So, you can take liberties with spelling, punctuation, grammar; you can write practically any way you like, so long as you understand the points your selves.  So, do not start writing at once, but create a synopsis of relevant points. A synopsis of what, a synopsis of relevant points. If you have been asked to write about happiness, you should not be talking about cow or bull or dog or other pets, which might be incidental; the pets maybe universal. You can say there are 70 percent people in the city of Chennai keep pets that may or may not be universal. But you cannot make very generalized points on topics like this.  Therefore, there have been professional essay writers. People Lend, Haldane Aldous Huxley, many others. There have been, essays have been written ever since, there is language. Not written, composed or written, because the technology of writing is fairly recent, so we cannot claim that ever since they have been written, they're recent, the history of written essays is rather recent. But the point here is, they think before they write, and they organize their facts in a manner such that it is always with them, at least as long as they write.  So, for example, in this case, we are under instruction, to create an example, and then you know, create a synopsis. Let us see.  Here is the synopsis again. Create a synopsis first. You need not know everything about any subject. There is no subject in the world which tells you: I will not open to you unless you proved yourself a scholar in all subjects; that is neither humanly possible nor desired, no need. But whatever we know, do we know for sure? So, synopsis may be a good occasion. For example, on a topic like this, unlimited happiness, shall we define the subject? What do you mean by happiness? Then some instances to show that on these moments we are happy, and on these other moments we are unhappy.  Maybe every birth made us happier, and every death made us unhappier. So, definition of happiness might change, instances of happiness might change, yet you must bring those examples, evidence and instances. Let us go to the next point then. The next point before me is: after labor rating the need for happiness we will have to define happiness. What do you mean? Suppose we want to give a friend 3 kilograms of happiness, even then I cannot do so unless I know where I can get a good healthy sheep or chicken or fish or anything because I want to give them a certain quantity of it.  So, happiness can differ from people to people. It is not eating fish alone that gives happiness; fish from where? Fish cooked by whom? Fish served by whom? All these questions may arise. In this world of cutthroat competition, there is so much emphasis on quality and saving every rupee, every penny. So, you must remember the fact that we have to write in a manner, which is succinct; which does not require anything from anyone else. It knows itself who it is, and then it can talk about other aspects. So, these are some points on synopsis.  How do you define happiness? What do you mean actually? Then what is empathy, antipathy? What is the meaning of cutthroat? Does it mean everybody is very rich or very successful only they can compete with one another? Or how is life and work together. You can have, you can bring in some statistical evidence national level maybe; so far, we have talked about the subject only at the particular level only in specific terms, but you can also bring examples from a larger field.  You can talk about whatever you like. Your examples from outside, the particular place where students belong to etcetera, etcetera; then elaborate cutthroat competition and say how the situation is in this place —all of these things.  Once we make a synopsis, half the job is done. It is said that for a good essay, good synopsis is important. Before writing an essay, if you sit down and make a synopsis you will end up writing good synopsis within the given words. But what is a synopsis? We are yet to define it. A synopsis is an overview. Imagine you stand on the roof of this building, perhaps you can see entire Chennai; but would you see the details of them? So, many people are defining a synopsis, many people have said that a synopsis is an overview, a synopsis is an overview.  Perhaps, in many ways, like imagine a village or a town where you go up the roof of, at the rooftop and look around, and you see the entire city in no time, entire city in no time. Actually, there is a wonderful joke. Somebody said that they wanted to see New York, all of New York in only 17 dollars. Then the taxi driver seems to have said I can show you an entire New York in 5 dollars.  This customer was very happy and said, yes, why not. Show it to me that way. Then he said, give me the 5 dollars this customer; this passenger gave him the 5 dollars then he said, "climb back to your flat and go on to the top of the 104-floor block of flats, and you will reach the top of this tower block, and you will see all of New York". Actually, he was talking about the World Trade Center, which no longer stands there. He said go to the top of the World Bank, World Trade Center and you will see all of Chennai in under 5 dollars.  Now, this was surely a joke. But we must remember the fact that from a height we can see the entire region. So, that is the meaning of a synopsis. A synopsis is an overview; what you get when you stand on the rooftop and look at the city all around the spread all around you. So, a synopsis is a similar thing, it is an overview of what you are going to say, not necessarily in the same order. Sometimes if you like you can change the order, but generally you can speak that way. So, it is an overview. Go next.  A good essay for reflection for instance, cannot have everything, so it cannot take everything. No way, that is not possible. But a good essay, particularly a good essay for reflection, must dwell upon some important points, some important things. They must not go on attended or neglected.  Besides designing a good simple, good synopsis, designing a good synopsis can help you write the best essay you are capable of writing. Please trust me. As Vivekananda said our abilities are hidden within us, all we need is somebody to come and uncover it so that it comes out. It is so true also of this essay. Whatever you want to say is already there in your head, but we do not use them at the right moment.  Use that time. If you have only 30 minutes to write an essay then out of those thirty minutes please, for god's sake, use at least 5 minutes to create a synopsis. You can say if I have given everything to only creation synopsis where am I going to write? My answer is the following. You see, you will write much more easily with greater felicity. As they say, and yet you will take fewer words that may be possible for, possible because of these techniques. Namely, that you say the same thing in fewer words; so that is why it requires practice.  If you make a good synopsis, it not only saves your time it also helps you produce the best essay that you are capable of writing. So, you need not wander in the dark, in a dark room, not knowing which way to go; you can trust yourself, think on a topic, give yourself some time, and it is highly unlikely that you will write less than the best possible essay. Provided you search your brain, search your mind, look into your own experience in the light of the template that you may have made. Next.  Let us do an activity for the sake of practice. Here is the rubric. Should there be only unlimited freedom? So, write an essay in about 200 words presenting your views on the subject. You can use any ideas, examples and evidence in support; that is the topic. I must also take inside and say that many school systems in Asian countries do not elaborate the topic in this manner. They simply give the topic and expect the students write, but it is always good to have a topic clearly elaborated.  Imagine you do not have a topic so clearly elaborated, and you still have to write upon those topics. How do you do it? The principles are the same. Number 1: first make a synopsis, first make a synopsis. Go next.  So, here for instance is a synopsis for the topic already given. What are you going to write? Print media, then electronic media, together they make the new media or the new mass media. Then there are movies. Then there are other sorts of stories, novels, plays, whatever we call by the name of creative freedom, the freedom of thinking. The more you think, the more you will find, you have things inside your head, and they are relevant to this topic. And you can make through this broken line, through this short hyphens or long dashes you can collect these points and keep them before you when you write an essay.  Actually, many school systems allow you to write an essay where you can write the synopsis first on top of the page, and then looking at the synopsis, you can develop one paragraph to each bullet point and you can make some good essays. Next.  Now, look at some problems. There, however, are some problems; even when you make a synopsis, it takes time. But we said that time invested in creating a synopsis is actually not a waste; it will save your time elsewhere, because you will write in a connected manner with felicity. But even while making synopsis many of us take a partisan view. We either forget to look at all aspects of the topic, or perhaps we do so deliberately, that is not clear. But many of us do not look at all possible aspects of a topic that would otherwise make it a great essay.  As a result, it declines into a partisan essay looks like you are talking for a particular side alone. Similarly, a good synopsis should reflect such comprehensive thought, it should show that all aspects have been taken into account in the synopsis that we saw. Please come back. In this synopsis, it is otherwise a good synopsis, covers many points, many important points. But does the writer talk about one individual person who is being advised here not to waste their time on electronic media? Who are being told that happiness would lie this way or that way, or that you need to have unlimited freedom? They forget. There is one another aspect to that essay is stated in the very first bullet point. Go back to the topic. The topic said, should one have unlimited freedom? And then it says censorship for mass media. So, this writer in our preoccupation with the topic with the content forgot to make a synopsis about a very important part of it, which goes like as follows, should one have unlimited freedom? Next.  So, many of us do not look at all possible aspects of topic. We also saw this while writing a précis. As a result, even when we do not want so we ended up making a - writing a partisan essay, writing a partisan answer. A good synopsis ideally should reflect this education, this thought, the experience, everything that you have gone through and everything that is relevant to the topic on hand; and then you will find you are able to write a good synopsis and therefore, a good essay.  If you sit down and think on the topic, some people think alphabetically. Ask to find an example they w ill say what first with A then with B, then with C, like this they make. Some others directly also go to examples. But without examples, your synopsis may not have the same strength. Over. Next.  So, look at this synopsis. This is what is being said. Next. Coming back to the point we began with; a good essay requires good preparation. What do you mean by preparation? We mean by before you start writing, you should jog your memory, and you should see how much I know on this subject? How much of what I know is relevant? If you can do these 2–3 things you will be able to write a great essay. Thank you very much, and good luck.

text: English 2 Dr. Om Prakash Guest Faculty Humanities and Social Sciences Indian Institute of Technology Madras Chennai English Vocabulary 01 Welcome to class. Today, we are going to talk about words and different ways to construct, coin, and add new words to the language. Can you imagine a language without words? Can we imagine? Words are the most significant component of a language. So, if you have the building blocks of a language, if you look at the building blocks of the language, we have sounds... what we call phonology-where we understand and study about sounds.  Then words and we study about the words in morphology. Then we have a combination of these words in meaningful chunks, strings and units, what you call utterances or sentences. Then these sentences, they combine to give us a paragraph. Then these paragraphs together combine to give a whole text.  So, sounds, words, sentences are the building blocks of a language. Then we understand the meaning, what we call semantics, and the overall understanding of the text or meaning is pragmatics. But out of all, these words are the key to understand a language. Now, words are so powerful. They hold... they sustain our ideas. They translate our ideas. Furthermore, they have key meanings, and they make us able to express ourselves.  So, words are so significant. And words as a class or dynamic, we keep on adding new words. I mean, look at this post IT revolution. How many new words are added to all languages of the world? In all languages, we have certain words related to computer technology added. It may be the case that they were not originally coined in the language. They have been borrowed from English, most of the words. Like, download for that matter, upload for that matter, are not new words, but because of this IT revolution and digital technology, this existing word extends its meaning, and it is being used as...like mouse in computers.  We use the word mouse. So, we all know what mouse is in a normal general meaning. But in computers, here mouse is a peripheral item. And for example, let us say window. So, window is an existing word. It existed before computers, and it has a different meaning. And window is a hole in a wall for ventilation.  But today, it has been extended to, and it is a semantic extension. So, a new meaning is added to the same existing word. Now, we know window is a software. So, all such kinds of things happen in a language with time and space. With different technologies and things. They require new words, and either we coin a new word, or we extend the meaning of an existing word. So, words are very dynamic in nature, and today we are going to talk about words.  Now, if you look at, let us look at a word called nationalization. Look at this word nationalization. Can we break it to different parts? Look at the internal structure of this word, how this word is coined or how this word is formed. So, we can definitely say something like nationalize. Can we break it further? We can say national. Can you break it further? We can say nation. So, you can see that nation as a word, which is a noun, we can form a word by adding all to the end of it, and we get an adjective out of it, the same word.  Then we add something else like size, and we get a verb out of the same word. And then we move further, and we add something to it, and we get again a noun. So, a single word leads to three, four words. Response, responsible, responsibility, responsibilityless, responsibilitylessness and they keep on adding, and we keep on making new words out of it. And every time, you find a different meaning to this word.  But not all combination of sounds or any combination of sound in a language can give you a word. Words are meaningful combination of sounds. So, those combinations and strings of sounds, which give you a definite meaning, then we know they are words. So, as we were breaking this one word into smaller parts, we come to a level where we cannot further break it.  We can say Na and ton, you cannot have two different. So, it can't be further broken because the more you further break it, meaning is lost. So, it has to have a composite meaning. So, we can break it to the limit or to the level where meaning is retained. So, meaning is there once, so not any combination of sound can be avoided. But is it the case that all combinations, like here, for example, all, what is it? Here for example, size, what is it? Here for example, ton? What is it?  This kind of things in the language, are they words? They are not words. But they are very essential element to modify a word, to change a word, to create a new word. They are very important elements. So, they do have contextual meaning. So, they may not have meaning on their own in their own.  In their own right, they may not be meaningful, but the function in such a way that if they attach to a new meaningful word, they extend, modify or change the meaning. So, they are also very essential part, but what did, what do we call them. Are they words or are they something else?  So, what we do? We call them morphemes, morphemes. We call them morphemes. That means a morpheme is the smallest unit of combination of the sounds. They have grammatical functions. So, morphemes are the smallest unit, and they form words. So morphemes are meaningful units which constitute a word, or as a grammatical unit they are instrumental in construction of new words.  So, like, for example, ton, size, all, we keep national, nationalized, nationalization. So, we can have two kinds of such categories of meaningful combination of sounds or what we call morphemes. And what are these? They are either, they are free. So, they can occur on their own, they have meaning on, in their own right, and they do not require any other thing for deriving meaning out of it. And one is called bound morphemes.  So, all these things that you see here, like suffixes added, are bound morphemes, prefixes added are bound morphemes. Prefixes, though, this string of sounds or combination of sounds, which are attached before the word. Prefixes-pre means before. And suffixes, those string of sounds, combination of sounds which are attached at the end of the word are suffixes.  So, there are some languages where you have infixes. Like these sounds, string of sounds, can be inserted in a word to make a new word, but English does not allow that. So, there are some, Malay, for that matter, a language allows infixes, but English does not allow infix. It allows either prefix. So, something added before the word or suffix, something added after the word. So, we have free morphemes and bound morphemes, there are two kinds of morphemes in English.  So, if you look at the classification of morphemes, you have free morphemes and bound morphemes. In free morphemes, you have lexical morphemes and grammatical morphemes. Let me tell you lexical morphemes. Lexical morphemes are those morphemes or combination of sounds or string of sounds which have meaning in their own right.  For example, dog. Combination of sounds in a particular meaningful way. Dog means dog. We know what does it mean. Cat, cow, fan. So, all these words, which we use independently, are lexical morphemes. They have lexical content. They have meaning. Grammatical morphemes which do not sustain on their own, but they are used in a sentence to make it meaningful.  Like articles a and e for that matter. Like conjunctions, and, if, whether... So, there are grammatical functional units of a language which are required to form sentences, clauses and utterances. If you look at bound morphemes, we have prefixes, because prefixes cannot stand on their own. We have suffixes, because suffixes cannot stand on their own. They are bound. They have to be glued to, attached to, added to a word. Then only they get meaning, or they give meaning. We derive meaning out of that.  Free morphemes can occur on their own, they have their own meaning, and they are free everywhere. What free morphemes can be of two categories. All adjectives, nouns, word that we use are free morphemes. But grammatical units like articles, conjunctions, exclamatory marking words, all these are bound morphemes, sorry, grammatical morphemes. Though they are free, but they are used in a structure or in a sentence to construct a larger chunk of sentence or data.  So, this is classification of morphemes —words, like free morphemes, like free words. And bound morphemes, this combination of sounds, which require a word to be glued, to be attached to. Otherwise, they do not carry any sense.  So, we will just have a very quick look at all these kinds of words and morphemes in the language, and this is, for the matter, this is true to any human language. It is not only true to English. You can think of your own mother tongue where you have words which are free and have meaning. There are some words which are required to form sentences, like articles and like connectors, like liners, like complementizers- if, that, whether -all these things. And also, you must have suffixes, prefixes, possibly infixes to create new words and categories.  You can think of that and then only you can relate to these explanations in English. So, we will talk about free or independent morphemes. So, such morphemes occur alone as word and have a meaning or fulfil a grammatical function, like, man, run. And is again, free morpheme. But it is a grammatically functioning morpheme because it is required to connect two ideas, two elements, two items in the language conjunction —coordinate conjunctions for that matter.  Now, this free morphemes are called Open class. So, free morphemes like nouns, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs, they are free morphemes-lexical morphemes, which have content or meaning in their own right. So, if I say dog, chair, fan, these are all nouns. So, all noun class is free morpheme. Verb-eat, drink, go, sleep, write, run-so these are verbs, and they all have a lexical content, meaning attached to them. You can derive meaning out of them, and they stand on their own. Then we have adjectives-black, fat, hot, cold. These are all free or independent morphemes like verbs. And adverbs-slowly, fast.  So, they are also called open class, in grammar. Open class. So they are open class of words. What do you mean by that? Open class of words. Open class of words refers to the ability of such words, where we can add more words. How many nouns can you add more to English? We cannot count. We have been adding nouns to English. New nouns, new words are derived, added to the language.  We are adding new verbs or extending meaning of existing verbs. We are adding adjectives. Furthermore, we can add adverb. So the number of, total number of nouns in a language, total number of verbs in the language, total number of adjectives in a language, total number of adverbs in language-they are expandable.  So, we keep on adding new elements in either or in any of these categories in the language, and we keep on adding up to it. We keep on adding. So they are called open class of words which have content meaning on their own. Then you have another category in the free morphemes like functional or grammatical morphemes.  So, can you guess if we have added any preposition to English in the last 50 years or 100 years? Or let us say conjunctions? What about articles a and the what about demonstrative, what about tactic markers, this, that, these, those, there, here? What about auxiliary verbs?  Like model verbs can, could, me, might, shall, should-have we added to it? Or what about pronouns -I, we, you?  You may say that the pronominal thy, thee, thou from old English, we have you in modern English. Except for that, do you see any other addition? Any addition to such class of words, like prepositions, an on, add, in, under, over, by, with? These sets of prepositions have we added to it or are we adding to it? Or can we add to it? Or articles like a and the?  We did not have any fourth one, we have not added any fourth one. Auxiliary verbs-verb be for that matter-is, am, are, was five, have we added to it? And model verbs like, will, shall, may, might, should, would, can-have we added? So, what does it mean? They are free morphemes, free words-they have a meaning.  But they have grammatical function. So they become meaningful and relevant when they are used in a larger chunk to create sentences, paragraphs, and texts. But they are a closed class of words. So, we do not frequently add new element to it. But nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs are open class of words-we keep on adding new nouns, new verbs, new adjectives, new adverbs. But here, in these categories, grammatical functional morphemes, we do not add. So that is closed class in any language. So, this is free or independent morphemes.  Moving on, this second type of morphemes is bound morphemes. Bound morphemes mean they cannot stand on their own. They need to be glued, added, or attached to a free morpheme. To derive a new word, a new category of words, sometimes, and we will see how we do that. But bound, and they are called dependent. They are dependent for their existence. They do not exist alone. Furthermore, they cannot have interdependent independent meaning.  Furthermore, they give meaning like her, her. So we say play and her, player. We say, let us say happy, but UN, a prefix added to it, we get an opposite meaning-unhappy. Able-adjustable, applicable. Main as a suffix. So contain, maintain. So, this is how such suffixes like r, size, UN...they do not have any meaning. But when they are added to a free morpheme or base, they give you a new category of words. They give you sometimes a modified form of the same class of word s.  So, they are called bound morphemes. And in bound morphemes, we have suffixes, prefixes, and infixes. So, the whole package is called affiliation process. Affiliation means you are fixing, fixing something to already an existing word. So, either you can add this before the word, or you can add after the word, or in certain languages like Malay for that matter, you can insert it inside the word to create, modify or derive a new word altogether.  So, types of affixes, we have three. Prefix-before the word, infix-inserted within the word, and suffix is added after the word. So, we can have three positions possible, and these are bound morphemes.  So, what are the functions? Why do we do that? Why do we need these affixes in a language? So, we need these affixes in a language to create a cluster of new words, sometimes to modify the meaning of an already existing word. So, we require these affixes. We call it affixes as a unit, as a uniform mode of addressing them.  Because suffixes, prefixes, suffixes, prefixes, or infixes. They are all together called affixes. So, we will use this term affixes, whether it be a suffix or it is a prefix. In English, we need to understand that way. So, you can have two kinds of affixes. One is called inflectional affixes, and the other is called derivational affixes.  Now, what do we mean by that? Derivation means we derive, and what do you derive? A new thing out of all the existing old thing. So, derivational affixes as a process of derivation in a language is very prolific, and the majority of words have a route, and from that route, we create a number of similar words, but sometimes with a different meaning.  So, when the category of the word changes, like from noun, we derive verb. From verb, we derive noun. From adjective, we derive noun. From noun, we derive adjective. From adjective, we derive verb. From noun, we derive adverbs. From verbs, we derive adverbs. So what we do? We derive a new word by attaching these affixes, whether before the word or after the word.  So, this is called that is why we call it derivational affixes or the process of derivation. So, in this derivation, it leads to multiplying the number of existing words in the language, and it is a very prolific process. So happy, opposite unhappy. Pleasant, opposite unpleasant. So, prefixing UN before pleasant, prefixing UN before happy.  Like verbs, I mean you are all using Facebook these days. Befriend and befriend. Sometimes, we coin new words. Befriend is not a regular word in English. But because of technology, because of tutor for that matter, because of Facebook and social media, we are deriving new words which are in vogue and very soon they will be part of normal conversation. But in social media, as a... as a practitioner of it, you must be aware, a number of new words you have coined. And they are in currency, and very soon they will be part of our, well, everyday repertoire, you never know.  Words have changed a lot. Like you brought a word from particular language, and then you customize it, assimilate it, and it becomes language, a word of your own language. And users even are not familiar and aware that this was borrowed in a different context with a different meaning.  So, semantic extensions, we are extending the meaning of these words, existing words in case sometimes, in place of creating a new word. All such wonderful things happen in language, pertaining to words, and the function of these affixes are either to create a new category of words or sometimes to maintain grammatical functions. We require creating new... variant of the word.  So, there are two things. Inflections create variant, it does not change the category. Derivations create another word, it changes the category. So, you can derive noun, you can derive adverb, you can derive adjectives, you can derive verbs. But when we talk about inflectional affiliation, that means, we do not derive a new category out of it. Instead, we have a variant of it.  Like for example, car, cars, chair, chairs, baby, babies, church, churches. What is happening? The class of word is not changing. What is changing? Only a variant. From singular, we are making it plural. It remains a noun. Class does not change, but we inflect it to make it plural. Go, goes. Verb, a variant.  So, this variant of verb goes with a plural marking suffix. It is strange. It is used for singular subject. So let me tell you, verbs are not singular or plural. But the agreement marker like ES in goes. It allows it to occur with first, third-person singular nouns. We derive, let us say comparative markers or like our superlative markers like est. Tallest, fastest. Fast is an adjective. Fastest, again is adjective.  But what happens we create two new variants. Faster and fastest. Inflectional pattern. It is an inflection. That means the category is not changing. It remains adjective as fast. It remains adjective as faster. Furthermore, it remains adjective as fastest. So, what we are doing, we are inflecting it to get a variant for a different purpose with a different semantic extension of it. So that is, that is what we need to understand.  So, if you look at inflectional affixes or inflectional affiliation process in English, we have eight kinds of inflections. Total eight kinds of inflection in English. Like s or ES, that we use as third-person singular marker of verb in present tense like speaks, writes, goes, runs, sleeps, teaches. This is one type.  Then, the second type or second kind of inflection processes, plural forming suffixes like s, and it has multiple forms, ES, IES, babies. So, regular plural marker to nouns. Then, the third one is apostrophe s. We use, do you remember apostrophe s. Ram’s, John’s. So, apostrophe s, which shows the genitive marker of possessive form. Then d or ed as a suffix, it is a regular past tense marker.  So, kill, killed. Go plus ed becomes went. Of course that is a different form. Write plus ed becomes wrote, but kill plus ed killed, jump plus ed jumped. So, this is another inflection type. Then third person, the third form of verb en. So, go plus en gone, write plus en written, eaten. Or then in gas a suffix. This is progressive marker.  So, cooking, eating, sleeping, going, jumping, etc. Then her, a comparative marker and then est, a superlative maker. So, these are the eight kinds of inflections we use in English, and they do not change the category of the class of word. So, a noun, even in singular or in plural, it remains a noun. An adjective, even in normal form, comparative form or superlative form remains an adjective.  Verb, even in past or past participle form, third form, or in progressive form or marked with s or ES, it remains verb. So, we need to understand that derivation process or derivational morphemes change the category of words and help us create new words. But, inflectional morphemes are moved for grammatical functions, and they require sustaining a grammatical structure. They do not change the category that we have to keep in mind.  And here are some quick examples for you. You can keep on practicing, or you can keep on deriving and breaking this word into smaller parts. And see whether you are using prefix, whether you are using suffix, whether it is inflectional morphemes, whether it is a derivational morpheme, you can test and check and play on your own. But let us have some quick examples of it.  In this case, look at noun-forming suffixes. That means we add something to a verb, it becomes a noun. Like assist, assistance. Assist, assistant. Confide, confidence. Complete or compete, completion or competition. Industrial, adjective and you can form a noun out of it, industrialist. Crude, an adjective. We can form crudity as a noun. Dry-adjective. Dryness- a noun. Free-adjective. Freedom-noun.  So, by adding a suffix to these adjectives or verbs, what we get noun. So that is a very prolific, productive process. Again you can keep on practicing and finding such examples in even in your own language. So, this process of suffixation is a very prolific process. So, some suffixes essentially form nouns. So, you add to verb, you get a noun. You add to adjective, you get a noun. These are the examples for you, moving on.  We can form adjectives out of verbs, out of nouns for that matter. Something like eat able-eatable, reduce- reduceable, differ-different, adjective, signify-significant, act-active, fashion- a noun- fashionable, an adjective, magic- a noun, magical-adjective. So, planet-planetary, affection-affectionate. So, you just use, add a suffix to these nouns and you find an adjective. You add suffix to these verbs, you find adjective. So, there are some suffixes, which essentially form an adjective out of a noun or a verb, and this is a very productive process. You can check, you can test, and you can practice.  Then, some verbs are formed out of nouns and adjectives like black-an adjective, blacken, solid-solidity or solidify, beauty- a noun, beautify-a verb, computer-a noun, computerize- a verb, length-a noun, lengthen-a verb. So, you can derive verbs, you can derive adjectives, you can derive nouns, and this is a very prolific productive process. You just need to understand that some affixes, some prefixes, or some suffixes are essentially used for forming nouns.  So, they are called noun-forming suffix. Or some suffixes are useful adjectives forming formation, so we call them adjective forming suffixes. There are some prefixes or suffixes used for deriving verb. They are called verb forming suffixes or prefixes. So, large-enlarge, en is a prefix, enlarge becomes a verb, large is adjective. So, you can just see and practice.  Let us say, asleep, befriend, empower, endanger, belittle, enlarge. So, we are using a prefix like a be, em, en, be, and we are prefixing it before a noun and getting a verb out of it. So, asleep, befriend, empower, endanger, belittle, enlarge, and this is how we form a new category of words. These are all derivational morphemes.  There are some affixes, which do not change the grammatical category, a class of words. Cigar-cigarette both are nouns.  So, big-biggie, hero -heroism, meaning does not change. Or if it changes, the same shade of meaning is maintained. So, such examples you can see and practice in your own language.  So, the world of words is beautiful, dynamic, and very fascinating.  They are very important component of a language. You cannot imagine expressing yourself without word. So, word are so powerful, and they have a beautiful internal structure. They are free morphemes, and they can be altered, modified, and changed. One word can be derived out of another word. So, you need to keep these things in mind and let us continue playing with the words and experimenting with our expressions. So, thank you for now. Thank you, bye.

title: Learning Softening (Knowing Vs. Using)
text: English – II Professor Rajesh Kumar Department of Humanities and Social Sciences Indian Institute of Technology Madras Learning Softening Welcome to the class. Today, we are going to look at one specific aspect of language, which is learning to use language. We call it Learning Softening. It requires our attention to several aspects. We are basically talking about the differences between knowing something and knowing to use what we know. If we keep this distinction in mind, then we can see it applies to language learning as well. Let us talk directly about language. Learning grammatical structure, learning sounds, words, sentences, intricate details of sentences is one aspect of learning a language. This is about; this is learning about the language, learning the details of languages and learning intricacies of language. But when we communicate with others, we need to know little more than these things because learning the structure and making attempts in learning these things is internal to us, internal to the human mind. However, all aspects of communication involve others.  So, when we speak, when we use the languages, we talk to others, we talk to another person or a group of persons or a large audience. We are only going to look at just a few aspects and see how learning about these makes a difference in how we speak. So, we are going to divide it into two parts, knowing and using, that is, learning to know about something, know something in details and knowing to use what we know. So, how we use what we know makes a lot of difference. Let us look at just a few aspects of it. But as a word of caution, I must say right up front that these are tentative suggestions. Your own presence of mind, your own intuitive understanding of society and the context in which you use the language is going to be the best help to you. However, what we are going to show, definitely going to help in forming certain patterns, are certainly going to be indicative of what we must know about the use of language.  Let us look at some of this. So, when we say we know, we know, when we learn the language, we know the following. We know about a sentence; we know that there are several types of sentences. We know there are word classes. Furthermore, we know there are word categories. Furthermore, we know there are grammatical categories. Furthermore, we know that there is a sentence that has got a subject and a predicate in it.  Furthermore, we know that that is not enough because we need to know about the composition of a predicate as well; that is, within the predicates, we may have objects, and we may also have adverbs. Objects are required elements; adverbs may not be required elements. These are the intricacies that we learn. We pay attention to them. We pay attention to examples. Furthermore, we see how our subconscious works with these things. Furthermore, we draw certain things from our own languages. And through this mechanism, we learn these details. We know about the complex sentences that when we have another sentence as an object of the word in the predicate, the sentence becomes a complex one.  We know that subject and predicate next to each other would not make a sentence. They are combined with certain other invisible and sometimes visible elements like agreement, which is basically a combination of number and person, gender is not so much important in English, tense in terms of present past and futures and certain aspects, all three of them, agreement, tense and aspects combine and work in a very intricate way to put subject and predicate together to make a sentence. When we talk about these things, they sound too technical. They are, they require a description of how the computation of language works within the human mind. That is what we mean when we say we know. As a child, when we learn a language before 15 years of age, this entire process is automatic. And when we learn, when we make an effort in learning after 15 years of age, we have to work on these things. And thus, we learn the language. But there is a purpose why we learn the language. The purpose is to speak; the purpose is to use. And when we use the language, we want to convey what we want to say, and more importantly, we want to convey what we want to say properly, adequately and appropriately. These parts properly, adequately and appropriately come from learning how we use them and this depends on the context.  And I am going to discuss a few contexts with you today to talk about this part of use of language in terms of properly, adequately and appropriately. So, appropriateness is the key factors in the use of language. We want to become impactful in communication, that is, when we speak with others. So, a combination of the two that is learning about the grammaticality, that is, accuracy with, and when we combine them with appropriateness, the two things together becomes, when we put the two things together, then we become impactful. So, to do so, we need to know how to say what we want to say. And the way we use the sentence makes all the difference. So, if we are not, if we are very grammatical and let me very let me be open about it, we need to be grammatical; we need to be accurate when we are speaking because if we are not accurate, if we are not grammatical, if we do not speak grammatically correct sentences, we leave a very strange impression and chances are that we will lose the audience, and we do not convey what we wanted to say impact fully, particularly when we need the audience to listen to us. Please pay attention to the footnote here. There are situations; there are contexts when we are in the audience, and we are required and forced to listen to and understand whatever the speaker is saying. I am not talking about that situation. I am talking about the situation when we need to convey ourselves properly, and we want full attention, and we want the audience, we want the hearer to get our message appropriately, accurately.  Under such circumstances, some of these things that we are going to discuss are going to be impact fully useful. In short, they can also be called certain aspects of common sense in language because the knowledge of context, that is the knowledge of use, is also something that children learn on their own. Grown-up people also learn them much faster when they pay attention to that. However, combining them, combining the appropriateness in a new language with the structural patterns of accuracy, is the key factor in this part. So, when we say about, when we talk about softening, it is not just how we look, how we present ourselves; it is about how confident we sound when we talk. And this confidence again requires both the sides proper, that is, accuracy on one side and appropriateness on the other side. And a proper combination of the two is going to make us impactful and confident. Hence, certain extra structural factors that we need to keep in mind are the following.  So, we are going to take few examples of context, and we are going to look at some of these helpful ways of saying things. So, what are, the contexts are like questions, suggestions or requests or when we express our opinion, when we are talking about some issues or when we have to say no, that is when we have to, we have a negative answer in the form of refusal. So, what are the things that we keep in mind in this context to make ourselves not sound so harsh or otherwise to the listener?  Appropriateness is a key thing because it comes from a careful knowledge of the context. See, when we speak, there could be two broad contexts in that. One could be informal, and the other is formal. However, I would like to bring this to your attention that even in the most informal contexts, we still need to employ a bit of formality. We need to bring in a bit of formality in the most informal contexts that we can imagine in our lives. That helps.  I will add a footnote here. When we speak, we want to sound natural. We want to sound as if we are speaking effortlessly. So, becoming natural requires looking effortless, but we need to understand that it takes a lot of efforts to look effortless. It can be consistency over a long period of time or preparedness to look effortless. Hence, I meant that even in most of the informal contexts, bringing in a little bit of formality makes it look impactful. Keeping that in mind, still, there is a distinction between informal and formal contexts. So, we are going to look at few imperative sentences, which are canonical examples of command and respect type of sentence. In our formal instructions, we have heard that there are some sentences which sound like command and there are some sentences which soundly request.  And I want to present this distinction to you with the help of context, with the help of description of context, and then you will be able to make a distinction that we need utmost care with these things. Our own intuition and instinct within a specific context can guide us if we are careful about the choice of our structure. So, look at this, there could be a situation when we can say, give me a glass of water. But, and that is considered as not so respectful, as an example of the command. And the second one, please give me a glass of water, is considered an example of a request. Now, what makes it a request? The fact that we are adding a term, a request term, please. It is a magical term in English, and we need to use this. But even in an informal context, if you use it, it does not make it really informal. It is okay to use please in an informal context as well. So, formally looking informal is going to make you look more impactful. We can say, the other example we can take is, meet with me at nine in the morning. We can use this sentence informally, casually. It is not a damaging sentence. It is not really a command, preferably and particularly when we know the context and the hearer, who we are saying this sentence to makes a huge difference. So, we can say, we can also say, please meet with me at nine in the morning. Mere absence or presence of please do not make it informal or formal, command or respect. It is how we say and to whom we say in what context that makes it either one of the two. And please keep in mind, even please meet with me at nine in the morning can be a good enough command. The only thing is you need to be imaginative enough for a context. You need to create a context. And that context can also vary from context to context. For example, imagine a situation, a war room type of situation where the top army general is meeting with his lieutenants, and they are discussing their strategies. At the end of that meeting, the general happens to tell a few of his colleagues, who are hierarchically junior to him in a certain sense, that please meet with me at nine in the morning. They can set up a whole new meeting or the general me wanted to know just a few of them at nine in the morning. Given the context of army discipline and a war room like situation, this is not just a request to the lieutenants. This can be construed as a good enough command in the sense that the hearer, the lieutenants, do not have an option to suggest an alternative type. So, the general says, meet with me at nine in the morning, or please meet with me at nine in the morning or the general can make it even more polite, is it possible for us to meet in the morning at nine, all these things and remain a command to the hearer. Think about a slightly different context that is not from the army context; let us imagine a context from the civil situation. These are the two terms that we use, civil and military situations. So, I do not mean civil in any other sense. So, in a civil situation with a hierarchy, it still applies the same way, but you can still imagine the possibility of suggesting some alternative of a meeting time. For example, if your boss tells you, meet with me at nine in the morning, or please meet with me at nine in the morning, though both are kind of mandatory required for you to meet with your boss in the morning, but depending upon what the boss chooses, what kind of sentence the boss chooses, you can decide your alternatives. So, in a civil situation, it is possible to suggest an alternative that, sir, is it, is nine-thirty okay. However, so the point that I am trying to make, these things are totally context-dependent. And it is the context that is to whom and where we speak, or we hear such sentences. I hope this command and respect type of situation is clear to us.  So, the it is, however, it is to that to make yourself sound softer in a normal situation you could use sentences like, could we meet at nine in the morning? Could we meet at nine in the morning, please?  And the third one, so look at this, look at the differences between the three, the third one is, I was wondering if we could meet at nine in the morning. They are, so, first one is definitely polite. The second one is more polite in that hierarchy. And the third one is it excessively polite a situation. Now, it is not that those who use the first one are not polite people. It is you; we need to pick one out of the three, depending on the context. For example, we can say, instead of saying, meet with me at nine in the morning, we can choose to say, could we meet at nine in the morning? However, if we are asking for a meeting where I am not in a situation to ask, to tell people to meet with me, we can say, could we please, could we meet at nine in the morning, please? That sentence can make you hearer think about your request more sympathetically. And the third one is definitely used to give an option to the hearer. And giving an option to the hearer in the sense that I was wondering if we could meet at nine in the morning, giving you an option to the hearer buys you certainty. You are being flexible, but by being flexible you are not allowing the hearer to be in a position to say no. So, look at the impact of this. If we are talking in a non-hierarchical situation or in a formal situation that is not really hierarchical, by using the one in the higher degree of politeness buys you more than you can actually get. So, it is in our favor to pick one over the other. However, we can determine the context in which we can pick one over the other. So that is the these are just a few soft versions available for us to use.  Sometimes we are in a context when we are either we solicit suggestions, or we are asked for suggestions or in a conversation, we find a situation where we need to suggest something. So, I just picked up a sentence. Imagine, in a even in an informal situation; your friend asks you a question, shall I invest in mutual funds? What could be your possible answers? No, you should not. Is a fairly grammatical sentence, a good enough suggestion, good enough advice. You can rationalize your advice. By the way, this has nothing to do with investment or no investment. I am just using a context. So, there is nothing wrong in saying so. It is a fully grammatical sentence, and this is where appropriateness comes in. But you would agree with me that such a sentence, no, you should not, it is rather more abrupt than a suggestion. It is a way to direct where the listener may not be ready to take that suggestion. So, what are our alternatives? A, it is too direct, it is too abrupt, though it is grammatical. So, here is the important part. Grammaticality is not enough. Grammaticality is required, but it is not enough.  Acceptability and appropriateness has to be topped up on grammaticality. So, this is where we see the actual role of acceptability. We talk a lot about grammaticality versus acceptability, and this is the key point where we see the acceptable role. Even in an informal situation you want to suggest something, and you want to be heard, one needs to find a less direct and impactful way. If you practice that, we are going to sound more impactful because the ultimate purpose of what we say must be, the sentences must be grammatical, but we want to leave an impact with those things. So, if you, however, you can express the same sentiments in different words saying, I think mutual funds are not doing good these days. You are not; how do we become direct, by not saying yes or no. How do we become not so direct? One way of doing so is by not saying yes or no; rather you just express your opinion which, so when you say, I do not think mutual funds are doing good these days, in that situation, we are, you are definitely indicating your answer towards a negative one. You can be a little more direct in that also and say if I were you, I would not. But think about it, it still sounds a little abrupt and direct because it has a negative word in it. You can say, if I were you, I would think several times about it. That is clear suggestion towards no, and it is not abstract, it is not direct. And it allows the hearer options. It allows the hearer to derive from your suggestions that you are not being imposing. You are not imposing your suggestion on your hearer, on your audience. That is key in making ourselves softer.  We can take a context from an issue. And so look, when we discuss issues, look at the situation, somebody comes to you, and it could be a hierarchical situation, because hierarchy in society is a very normal thing. Society is excessively hierarchical. There could be contexts where we can create a non-hierarchical situation. We discuss those things at some other point, but let us look at, let us focus on the main point in discussing issues. Somebody comes, somebody has sent you a report. You need to meet with a group of people, and you need to discuss that. But before that, it so happens that the person who has sent you a report wants to say or happens to say that, sir, I have submitted my reports on accounts. Hope you liked it or hope you had a chance to look at it. What is the purpose of this information? There are several purposes, but two of them are quite clear. One is the person wants you to know, even though you already know, that that person has finished the job. Mind it; it is also one of the informal ways of saying something when you run into each other, this is, that itself could be an instance of softening ourselves and understanding context, understanding situations and what to say in that situation. You do not, you may not want to compliment the person on his dresses, or you may not want to say anything else; rather you would want to say something that is common between the two of you.  Hope you liked it. You are giving an option. Hope you had a chance to look at it. You are just checking if that person has to say something. Then that person and tells you, you have made a mistake in calculations, means yes, I have taken a look at it. I had a chance to look at it. You have made a mistake in calculations. You have ruined it. Either one of the two responses or one of the two is devastating in nature. This is, these are grammatical sentences again for the purpose of discussing. There is nothing wrong in, nothing ungrammatical about these sentences, but they are not appropriate sentence in the context because your purpose is not to devastate your listener. You can express the same thing in different ways, and we can be more creative, wiser and use our knowledge of the context and our knowledge of the society to put that for softening, how we say the same thing.  We can say you seem to have missed a few things. May I suggest revisiting? Is it possible for you to relook at this and send it to me again? You are conveying the same message that there are some problems with the reports that you have sent. And if you want my opinion on that, may I suggest some revisit of that? The message is loud and clear, but it is way softer; it is not devastating. Now, this is where people say, understanding these parts are extra grammatical, extra-linguistic in the sense that it is not really about language, it is not really, understanding these aspects are not really embedded within language, but they are understanding the context, understanding the society is not really part of how we learn the language. That is not really true. Understanding communicative competence, understanding how we communicate, how we remain impactful, how we do not lose people must be one of our goals in communication. You do not want to lose your audience. The least that we can say is when somebody talks to you, at the end of the conversation, you do not want the hearer, the audience to feel bad. Even if it was not so pleasant, you can have a good conversation. You can give the feel of a good conversation to your speaker, to your hearer, as a speaker.  At this point, it is important to be again grammatically accurate plus communicatively appropriate. This, the second part comes only after the first one. So, the other response could be, it appears to me that calculations do not add up. Could you please take a look at it again? This is a detailed comment on the report. So, these are the ways of becoming softer. You can take your, use your own intuition and see which one would you prefer in, given a situation.  Yet another context, refusal, which is basically saying no, is a slightly tough one. People usually do not want to say no, but more often than not, we have to say that. It is not difficult. You can say that. But it requires a skill to say no without having said no. And again, that is the combination of the two linguistic skills as well as communicative confidence. To build your communicative confidence, you need that communicative skill. So, if you have a question, somebody runs into you and asks you, can we go for a cup of tea? What are your options? You can either say yes or no. How do you say that? You, depending, again, depending upon the context, you can choose various kinds of answers. Could you please bring me some storybooks on your way? This is asking for a favor, maybe not in so nice way. Look at the sentence. It is a very nice request. Could you please bring some storybooks on your way? If you happen to say no to both, what are the ways of becoming creative?  So, we can say things like; I have a lot of stuff pending to take care of. You can say more things, but this much is good enough. It says no without saying no. That is, it says, it gives the same sense, just that we are not using a negative sentence. It is still an affirmative sentence, but it is; it gives the sense of no. I have a lot of stuff pending to take care of. Hope you would not mind. What would you not mind? You would not mind the sense that is emerging out of it as a response to the question, can we go for a cup of tea? Which is no. No, I cannot. Also, keep in mind, in order to express refusal, you do not have to say the factually correct information.  The response to the other question, could you please bring me some storybooks on your way? You can say, I will try my best. It is a good sentence, it is a grammatical sentence, it is a short sentence. But when you say that, it gives the sense of, it says, I will try, but it clearly gives a sense that chances are you will not bring. If you want to bring, employ a little more clarity in that, you can say, the shop seems to have moved, as I could not find it. This says a lot about it, but basically, it is more that, more of no. I am not sure if there is any bookstore on my way; this is way more direct. Now, I am not discussing the ways of, to use the word lying, but the knowledge of the context and the situation in which you need to use these sentences would probably require you to say some of these things. It is still useful in the sense that saying, no, I cannot bring or no, I cannot go for a cup of tea, though grammatical, but not appropriate sentences, would not buy you much. So, these are not the ways of lying, but these are ways of communication where the idea is to convey the sense as a response to the question. And particularly this is a useful skill in saying no to something.  So, again, these are just a few situations that I created, just a few sort of possible answers in those contexts. I have tried to describe the context to you. But as I said, the things that we have discussed for today is; basically, we need to be aware of the context. And there is no specific rule that makes us aware of the context, and being and becoming softer in communication is really a social skill, but ultimately, but the essential thing for our communication, for becoming impactful. It is a social skill, requires linguistic competence and a combination of the two that is the combination of grammatical rules, and these kinds of social skills makes us effective communicator. These things might sound as cliché to you, but keeping them in mind time and again and thinking about strategies is going to help. Now, I would like to draw your attention to the following. You might have already been doing these things a lot. This is not something that you have to wait to learn to do. Other people may be using these sentences with you. Here on, I would like you to pay attention to these sentences, these contexts, and see, can you be more creative, innovative? Do people become more creative and innovative? Make a list of those situations, make a list of the possible answers in those situations and see how impactful that in turn makes you in becoming in deploying communicative effectiveness to develop your confidence and communication. title: Tense Aspect Mood
text: English-II Professor D r. Om Prakash Guest Faculty, Humanities and Social Sciences Indian Institute of Technology Madras, Chennai Welcome to class. Today we are going to talk about Tense, Aspect, and Mood. Tense is a very significant and very important grammatical phenomenon in any language, and we will also talk about aspect, which is another significant phenomenon and, of course, mood. So, before we begin, let us understand that verb in any language is the most important constituent of a sentence. Most important. Why is it the most important? Because for any sentence, verb is the nucleus.  So, sentences are structured around the verb. Verb is a very important thing. You cannot have a sentence without a verb. Other arguments like, you know, subject. Important, of course. Verb, important. Direct object depends on whether the verb is transitive or not. Not necessarily, you have direct object all the time. You can have a you can have something like, you know, this is my watch, I have a watch. So, sentence like this or Shelley runs fast. You know, you don’t have to have an object here, direct object here, but you cannot imagine a sentence without a verb.  So, this is the most significant and important phenomena. And verb is the storehouse of a lot of information. So, it contains a lot of information about so many other grammatical elements. So, almost all languages, all human languages, require a verb to form a sentence, and that is why I said that verb is the most important thing in a sentence, and they express action, describe an event, or establish a state of being.  And verb bears the markers or the characteristics of tense, aspect, and mood. So, we get a lot of information from the verb. A single word can contain so many, so much of information, so many things. So, the role of verb is very crucial in a sentence. So, when we talk about tense, when we talk about aspect, when you talk about mood, you know, verb remains at the center of all these constructions not only in English, but also in other languages as well. You can think of your own mother tongue, and can you have a sentence without a verb? Just think.  So, today we are going to talk about tense, aspect, and mood. If you look at the timeline, if you draw, let us say a line. So, we draw a line and let us say this center is present, then on the left, we have past, this is present, and this is a future.
