Command on grammatical rules and sentences, familiarity with the expressions only, or are we talking about a total package where you are good at vocabulary, you are good at structures, you are good at pronunciation, and you are competent and good at understanding the situation in which these are used?  So, are you familiar with the forms only or are you familiar with the functions as well? Communication is all about the combination of form and function of the language. We may have good command of a wide variety of sentences. You may be fairly good in pronunciation, but all these are complimented with your ability to use these in appropriately, in appropriate socio-cultural contexts. So, what is the role of context in communication? That is what we are going to talk about today. This idea was discussed by Dell Homes a linguist, a socio-linguist in mid 60s, and he named it ethnography of communication, and he created an acronym just to sound fancy and effective, he created the acronym speaking and each of the letters of the word speaking, ‘S’ stands for let say scene and setting’ ‘P’ for people; ‘E’ for end; ‘A’ for act. So, you know ‘K’ for keys, ‘I’ for instrumentality. So, ‘G’ for genre.  So, this word speaking is not a normal word, it is an acronym in this sense, we need to understand, and we will talk about it gradually when by, when we progress in our discussion. So, he talked about communicative competence. Some of you may be familiar with this idea of communicative competence.  But when we say competence, we are referring to the tacit underlined knowledge of the speaker about the language. Opposed to communication, another idea is performance. So, competence and performance; opposed to competence we have performance. So, competence and performance. So competence refers to your underlying tacit knowledge, your potential, your ability and performance refers to the actual act.  So, you may be very competent, but it has to be reflected in your performance. To that extent, Dell Homes merges his two binary ideas. So, he calls it communicative competence that means, your performance is not detached from your competence. Your performance reflects your competence. So, he coined his term communicative competence to contrast and oppose with the idea floated by Chomsky about linguistic competence.  So, Chomsky and linguistic competence refers to the computational aspect of language, the tacit knowledge of the structures of the language of the native speaker, which is not interrupted by external things like memory loss or any kind of problem and impediment. So, he imagines an ideal form of speaker and listener and ideal speaker and listener and the tacit knowledge of language in terms of structure. But that was found to be inadequate explanation of language and properties of language as far as people like Dell Homes is concerned, and they placed a lot of thrust on performance aspect as well. So, knowing a language does not only include knowing the structures and the rules of grammar, but the appropriate use of them in appropriate socio-cultural context.  So, knowledge of language is combination of both, confluence of both, and this is how he coins the word ‘communicative competence’. Whether you are able to communicate properly or not, that determines your level of competence. So, today we will talk about the context, role of context in effective communication.  So, your knowledge of language is the combination of your knowledge of the formal properties of language that means the structures, vocabulary, pronunciations, rules of grammar and also the functional aspects of it, how they are applied in the real-world situation.  So, Dell Homes comes up with sixteen components, which are crucial and important in a conversation. He calls it Sixteen Components Applied to Discourse. You know, so, how they are important, always remember language is socio-culturally rooted. When you talk to a set of people, we not only understand and discover a new set of expression, words and sentences, at the same time, you also discover a new set of cultural norms, communication patterns, their beliefs, conventions. So language encodes culture and social configuration and patterns.  So, they are intertwined. Language and culture are intertwined. And that is why when you are communicating, it is important that you are familiar with these cultural norms, with the social patterns and the contexts in which you communicate. So, ultimately who speaks? The speaker. To whom you speak? The receiver. What you speak? The message. How you speak? The manner. Why we speak? The objective and goal, and when you speak? The timing, sequence. So, who speaks what to whom, when and why, and how is the whole package, that makes you an effective communicator. So, it is important to understand the role of the speaker, location of the speaker in the social space. It is important to understand the audience: who is going to receive your message, who is your communication partner. It is important to understand what we are going to communicate, the content. Why you are going to communicate: your intent and objective of the goal of communication.  When are you going to communicate: the timing of it. How are you going to, go to communicate: the manner, formal or informal, the sequence, the genre. So, all this matter. So, when we say ‘I know English, I can communicate in English’ that means, you are familiar with these components and elements of communication.  So, Dell Homes comes up with 16 components, and what are these? Let us say message form, what is the form of the message; then message content, the content of the message the theme of the message; then setting, the social situation and space where this communication is taking place; then the scene, the social context in which it is taking place; then a speaker and a sender, so the communication partners, their status, their position, their dynamics; and then addressed, hearer and receiver, the audience, addressee; purpose, the goal of communication, the intended outcome of the communication; key, the social clues that you get out of the tone out of pauses out of other factors which give you social clues. So, that refers to keys; then channels, what channels we choose to communicate; then the form of speech; then norms of interaction and this is purely cultural and social; norms of interpretation, and finally genre.  So, we do have a different pattern when we communicate to our seniors, our elders; we do have different patterns of communication when we communicate to our juniors, our colleagues. So, the degree of formality garage. And the choice of words, the choice of sentences, the choice of utterances, they vary. You cannot use the similar style with a variety of people. Then, we have domain-specific words and sentences and expressions, they are called register. So, we have to pay attention to the register you are using like when we are talking about a formal meeting of, let us say medical practitioners, the language will be different. The jargon technical words will be different from common situation, normal situation. Let us say you are talking in the, in the meeting of engineers, the register will be different.  So, engineering, medical, arts, science, technology. So, domain-specific technical words, sentences, expressions and norms that we follow. Then we have our own style of using language, we have personalized style, individual-centric styles; idiolects, individual centric variations that we have. And overall, the norms of the patterns of communication in a particular society. In some societies, for example, overlapping speech or unwarranted interventions is considered rude.  But in some societies, it is quite common, two, three people can speak at a time and still communication goes on. The way you open your conversation is cultural. The way you attach degree of formality to the communication act, it is purely cultural. How you intervene, how you disagree, how you agree, how you oppose. So, lots of nuances, these nuances must be known to us.  So, Dell Homes lists these Sixteen Components Applied to Discourse, or an extended conversation. And what are the sixteen? Number 1: message form. Number 2: message content. Number 3: setting. Number 4: scene. Number 5: speaker and sender. Number 6: address or. Number 7: hearer, receiver or audience. Number 8: addressee. Number 9: the purpose. Number 10: again, purpose. So, in first it is a common outcome, the actual outcome of the act. In the second, we say goals objectives.  The next key, then channels, then forms of speech, then norms of interaction and norms of interpretation and genre. You might have seen in the case of cross-cultural communication where you have the participants in a communication at, from different socio-cultural backgrounds, a lot of confusion happens at the level of interpretation. People interpret similar thing differently. So, that is also important. As a speaker, you should be familiar with the potential interpretation of a message by a variety of different people. So, you have to, need to memorize this variation. So, Dell Homes comes with these sixteen components.  And then he brings out an acronym to accommodate all these sixteen into eight components, and he creates an acronym SPEAKING. So, that it also looks like an acronym and a word ‘speaking’ to sound fancy and effective. So, what is that speaking model?  Look at this. Speaking, ‘s’ refers to setting and scene. ‘P’ refers to participants. ‘E’ refers to end, ‘k’ refers to key, ‘i’ refers to instrumentalities, ‘n’ refers to norms and ‘g’ refers to genre. So, we will talk about each of these components and their significance in communication. When we learn a new word, we learn three things together.  Number 1, spelling and pronunciation. If we learn a word orally, of course pronunciation. If we learn a word in writing, spelling. So, the first component of a word is spelling and pronunciation. The second thing that we learn is the meaning of it. And the third thing that we learn with a word is the context in which it is used.  So, when you learn a new word, we have to have this understanding of these three components of a word. Spelling and pronunciation number 1, meaning of the word number 2, and the context in which these words are used, that is number 3. So, when we learn a language, we actually learn the formal properties of language.  So, vocabulary, pronunciations, same sentences, meaning of these words and sentences, expressions. At the same time, we also learn the functional properties of language. So, that enables you to use the language effectively. So, this static knowledge of formal properties actually does not help. What helps, the combination of the two aspects formal and functional properties. So, Dell Homes talks about functional aspects of it: how to use it in a sociocultural context, and what are the components and attributes which are important to understand as a communication partner or as a communicator.  So, he comes up with this list of eight components which are very crucial in applied conversation communication discourse and these eight have been chosen and named in such a way that the first letter of these eight components create an acronym which is known as SPEAKING, setting and scenes, participants, end, act sequences, keys, instrumentalities, norms and genre. And these eight create an acronym SPEAKING, and it is called the SPEAKING model.  Now, what do you mean by setting and scene? So, setting refers to the time and place of a speech act and in general, to the physical circumstance. Scene is a psychological setting, or cultural definition of setting, that includes the characteristics such as the range of formality and sense of play or seriousness. You might have seen certain people are very particular about the degree of formality. Degree of formality does matter, that attaches value to what you say.  So, setting the speech event also refers to the location of participants and any physical barriers that may be present. So, it basically, scene refers to a socio-psychological, physiological, physical and psychological both location in the social space, cultural space of the speaker and of the listener or a receiver. Where do you stand, where you are located and then the social norms, cultural norms, which plays a role in the background? So, that is called setting and scene. So, the socio-cultural context in space where the communication happens.  Then the next is participants: the speaker and the audience, that can be distinguished as addressee and other hearers. So, when considering the participants in a speech event, one should consider implicit and explicit rules about who is and can and should be involved. What expectations are established for the participants, who is speaking, who is being addressed.  So, the role of the participants, your role as a speaker, your role as a listener, if it is a group communication, the role of other participants of the communicative act, and who can speak what, to what extent, who is allowed, who is not allowed: these are norms which are socio-cultural. You might have seen in the most of the time, in our family affairs as a child, we were rebuked and scolded by elders not to speak when two people are talking. So, even if you are present there, you are not talking. You are simply receiving, but at the same time, you are muted in the sense that you are not supposed to give feedback.  So, it is, the communication is determined by the role and the relevance of the participants in the act. So, ‘p’ means participants, refers to the speaker and the audience and the norm and set rules for participations. So, that everyone can speak, everyone can respond.  So, according to your socio-cultural location and in the socio-cultural space as the participants, it is determined whether you are supposed to speak or not, what you are supposed to speak, how you are supposed to speak, to what extent you can intervene, these are all important in effective communication when any conversation in a group takes place.  Then he talks about the ‘ends’. Every communication act has an objective particular goal. It is specified, unlike gossip, you can have gossip with anyone anytime and about anything. So ‘ends’ in this model refers to the purpose of a communication, the goal of communication and what is the actual outcome of it.  Then we move to ‘act sequence’ and it refers to the form and the order of the event. So act sequence refers to the sequence of speech acts that make up the event. The order of speech acts greatly influences the speech event. So, act sequence for an event also orients the participants to social cues. Important aspects of act sequence include turn taking and interrupting. So, as the communication, as the conversation progresses, the sequence becomes important. So, who speaks, who takes the lead, who initiates the conversation, and then when the other participant or other partners is involved, how you interrupt, how you intervene, whether the socio-cultural norm allows you to interrupt, whether the socio-cultural norm allows you to intervene, these are all factors in this speech act. At the same time, turn taking and turn given, it is your communication strategy where you take the turn, at the same time, you also finish your talk, finish your thing, allow the other person to speak. So, it is a kind of negotiation going on continuously, it is a very dynamic relationship and negotiation going on. So, communicative negotiations are going on, who will speak what when, how, who will take the turn, who will be silent, who will be continuing, who will interpret, how you will interpret. So, these are all complex negotiations that happen all the time during the speech act.  Then we move to key and key refers to the clues that establish the tone, manner or spirit of the speech, clues that establish the tone manner of spirit of the speech act. You get clues when you progress in conversation, we look at the direction to which this communication is going, and we get a lot of clues with tone, pitch and other metalinguistic nonverbal cues that help you understand the direction of the communication, the intent of the communication and possible outcome of the communication. So, we have to be very alert and paying attention to these keys which hint you towards the direction this communication is going.  Then instrumentalities. What do we mean by that? So, instrumentalities refers to the form and style of speech and these include the method of communication with the writing, speaking or signalling the language or dialect whatever variety you are using, your style register. So, these are all instrumental: the language you choose, the variety you choose, the style with which you speak this is a selection of words. So, the form and the style becomes instrumental and very significant in your conversation and effective communication.  Then we have norms, and these are socially governed, culturally governed. So, socio-cultural norms determine the shape, size and outcome of the communication act and conversation. So, when it is okay to speech, speak, who should listen and who should speak, when is silence preferred, how loud is too loud? When speech, what speech should be used in conversation and what topics are appropriate and acceptable?  These are all socially, culturally governed factors. For example, let’s take taboo words. For example, let’s take taboo themes. So there are certain topics and themes, we do not discuss publicly. There are certain topics or themes, we do not discuss formally. So, these are all cultural norms, something that you may find taboo and prohibited, may be a simple thing for other culture.  So, you find other people talking about it, and you find inhibition, you have inhibitions, and you feel inside about it. So, this is culturally governed, socially governed. So, our social conditioning, our cultural conditioning, our understanding of the society or culture determines all these factors.  So, when it is appropriate to speak, when it is appropriate to be silent, what are the topics that we should discuss, what are the themes and topics that we should refrain from? How loud I can be and how loud can be not loud? What is the threshold? So, that refers to norms in speech event or communication.  And genre is the final thing. So, what kind of, what is the content, what kind of speech or what kind of speech event is going on? Is it the gossip? Are we cracking jokes? Is it conversation, simple conversation, or intense discussion and debate? Is it instructive and moral instructions? Is it didactic? So, it can be anything and accordingly, we need to customize.  So, we need to customize our conversation, our communicative style, our communicative strategy according to the genre. So, finally if we look at this SPEAKING model, it gives us an understanding of the context in which a speech event takes place. And the role of context, the role of setting, the role of scene, the role of participants, the objective, the goal, the form and order, socio-cultural keys and clues, language as instrument, the socio-cultural norm in progression of the speech act, and the genre. These eight elements determine the effectiveness of our communication.  So, as a communicator, we need to pay attention to these eight. So, finally we can understand that as a speaker or as a communicator, I have to keep in mind who speaks what, to whom, when, why, and how. These six questions we must understand. So, with this, we conclude, and we’ll continue our discussion about the socio -cultural context, appropriateness of language, selection of words, selection of sentences, appropriate expressions, and cross-cultural understanding in communication in our upcoming classes. This is it for now. Thank you very much.

title: Barriers to Communication
text: English - II Professor Doctor Om Prakash Guest Faculty, Humanities and Social Sciences Indian Institute of Technology, Madras Welcome to class. Today we will talk about certain challenges and impediments that we face while communicating. George Bernard Shaw said the greatest illusion about communication is that it has taken place. So, the moment we send the message, the moment we tell someone something, write someone something, and we have this belief that it has been communicated.  So, the act of communication at the end of the first participant or the sender of the message is believed to be completed because you have sent it, you have shared it. But did it really happen, does your message get across the way you originally wanted, is the receiver of your message able to decode, understand the message you originally intended to send, that is the question. So, despite all your honest and earnest efforts, the message may be misinterpreted, there may be distortion and the intended message may not be communicated. So, apart from understanding the form and functions of language, it is also important to understand the context in which you communicate and the outcome, the ultimate communication that happens.  So, today we will talk about certain obstacles and barriers that we may face while communicating. Though such barriers cannot be listed exhaustively, but we will try to understand some generic and general impediments, the obstacles or the barriers. So, if we are aware of these barriers, we can minimize the degree of subjectivity, and we can be objective and communicate effectively. So basically, I am going to talk about communication strategies and language use. So, knowing English, knowing English grammar, having good vocabulary, they are important. But it is equally important to have the skills to use them appropriately in an appropriate socio-cultural context and that is what is the theme and the thrust of this class.  Moving on, so we are going to talk about barriers to communication. So, we can have multiple barriers, any kind of impediment which implies any hurdle in the free flow of message and interpretation, sending of the message and interpretation or interpreting of the message is known as barriers. Now, it can be multiple, but we can cluster them or categorize them into five distinct classes or categories of barriers, and they are physical and mechanical barrier, those barriers which are not in the control of the speaker and the listener. Second is the language and semantic barrier. So, there are certain linguistic items elements, for example, structure, vocabulary, selection of words, linguistic differences, so these are the things that they create a lot of misunderstanding, and they become a barrier to communication. Semantics means, so the word that you select and the general understanding of the word. So, meaning is contextual; it is how context becomes a barrier, how inappropriate selection of words may become a barrier. Then we have socio-psychological barriers, so how the social and cultural background of the communication partners, their attitudes, their preferences, their likings, disliking, biases, they all become impediment in effective communication. So, we will talk about sociopsychological barriers. Then you will be working in organizations, sometimes organizational hierarchy, cultural patterns, organizational structure, the rules, they all may act as an impediment in certain contexts. So, they are called the barriers which originate because of the organizational structure, cultural patterns and practices, so they are called organizational barriers; we will talk about them. Then as an independent communicator we do have our personal barriers. So, we can have five distinct categories, physical and mechanical barrier, language and semantic barriers, sociopsychological barriers, organizational barriers and personal barriers. And why this is important to understand these barriers? Because if we know these barriers, then we can work towards minimizing the if impact of these barriers in our communication exchanges, in our language exchanges, in our communication patterns, we can minimize these barriers. You might be familiar with the process of communication; it is a general knowledge everyone knows about it, so that there is a sender, there is a receiver, there is a message. So, the sender encodes the message in a particular code, let us say in English for example, the receiver decodes the message and the receiver encodes the feedback and sender decodes the feedback. So, this is how message and feedbacks are exchanged, and the communication cycle is complete. So, it looks so simple when you look at the process, it looks so simple that you speak something other person interprets it and that is it, you get the feedback that the person has understood and that is it. But a lot of other things happen between sending and receiving, between encoding and decoding.  Size of the message, clarity in the message, brevity in the message, objectivity in the message, simplicity in the message, intelligibility in the message and usually utility of the message, they are all attributes to have effective messaging and communication, they are attributes, effective attributes.  So, we need to have our message or our sentences or our text that we are going to communicate, precise, focused, straightforward, objective, easy to comprehend, simple and useful for the receiver or the reader or the listener. Because if the listener does not find any value in what you are saying, if the reader does not derive any value out of what you are writing, then the message is not received, it is ignored.  So, it is important to maintain brevity, you have to be concise, the message must be small. When I say small does not mean one or two sentence, it can be long message but simple sentences, small sentences, so it had to be compact, no deviations, it has to be compact, concise, straightforward, to the point, objective. When we say objective that means we are trying to be non-ambiguous. So, you should not give space for the listener or reader to interpret the message, so it is open-ended, it should not be open-ended message, the message, the focus of the message must be very clear and specified. Then it should be unambiguous, no ambiguity, no multiple meanings; it has to be straightforward.  Then it has to be intelligible that means you have to understand the listener or the reader who is going to receive a message. So, the potential of your reader, of your audience must be known to you, the level of your audience must be known to you, and you have to customize your message according to that, so that is very important. So, we will talk about these barriers, and then we will get back to how we can overcome these barriers. Always remember communication is an art, it is an art, and you have to inculcate the best practices gradually. It does not come to you so quickly by mugging up and memorizing thousands of new words, low-frequency words by sounding intellectual by using complex sentences; it does not work.  What works is how intelligible you are, how focused you are, how straightforward you are and how quickly you connect with your audience that is important. Connecting with the audience is important, your reader, connecting with your reader, connecting with your listener is important. And why? Because the moment you connect that means you both are at an equal plane and your job becomes easy; you can be effective in your communication pattern, in your communication act, you can be very effective. Effective communication requires certain attributes that we must be familiar with and practice. So, let us begin with physical and mechanical barriers.  Now, what do you mean by physical and mechanical barriers? Noise, any kind of physical noise around, the surrounding in which you are communicating, any kind of disturbance, you may not have control on this, but it definitely creates problems in effective communication, effective exchange of messages, any kind of mechanical disruption will be problematic. Timing of the message, the distance of the communication partners, the distance between communication partners specifically in terms of face- to-face communication, external disturbance and noises around and the information overload. So, the pace of delivery and pace of reception that has to be balanced; otherwise it becomes a barrier. So, when we say overload, that means we are sending a lot of message and text, sharing a lot of message and text beyond the normal capacity of your audience. So, your audience may not be at that level, and then there is a mismatch in sending and reception of the message, and that creates impediment, that becomes a barrier because it does not matter how intellectual you sound and how abstract you are in your message, how intelligent you appear in your message. If your message is not interpreted by your audience, your reader, your listener, then message has no value because always remember communication is a two-way process. It is an exchange and progression of ideas between these two partners. And this exchange of ideas and sustained progression are possible only when both of them meet in the equal plane. So, that is why we say that communication is you oriented, you oriented, listener oriented, audience oriented, not I oriented. What I want to communicate is important but more important is that whether my audience is able to receive that message properly or not. So, you have to customize your message to meet the efficacy and capability of your receiver or the audience to receive and that is why it is important to customize the message according to the audience. So, you that means the receiver becomes the central point of your all thrust, and you have to customize and design your message according to the user of it, according to the receiver of it, according to the listener or reader. So, that is why, but there are certain things over which we have no control like the noise, disturbance, mechanical problems, interruptions. So, we put all such kinds of things in the physical and mechanical barrier. So, those impediments which are present around in the physical environment and which create any kind of disruption they are put in this category physical and mechanical barrier.  Then we move to the most important and second category that is language and semantic barrier. We are talking about let us say English, now English remains the same language all over wherever it is used, broadly the rules of grammar are similar, and a range of vocabulary is also similar. But why the communication in English in let us say India and then in Canada or in Britain or in America or in Caribbean islands or all over we all have different communication patterns, all the Englishes that we are talking about are different because the speakers are different, audiences are different, language remains the same, but there is a difference, and these cultural differences create a lot of barrier and misunderstanding. So, language as a code may be similar or same, but the functions of these linguistic items are culture-specific. So, if you look at structures of English in India, Indian English structures they can be ambiguous and confusing for a British receiver, though both of you are using English, you are familiar with the structures, you have vocabulary, you are communicating in English, but these cultural items creep in and create a lot of barriers. So, these linguistic items become a barrier cross-culturally. Language becomes a barrier when your message is not clear. Translation is the most challenging thing, translating an idea from one language to the other is very challenging because there is a cultural element attached to it, and you may not find an equivalent of that expression while translating, or you may lose the essence of the message in translation, language becomes a barrier. Your assumptions, when your assumptions are not specified, your intentions are not known, then it may be ambiguous and confusing, and it may create a communication gap on part of the receiver, so assumptions must be clear, connotations must be clear, context must be clear, the metaphorical use of language must be appropriate. For example, in English we say time is money and the Hindi equivalent of time is money is ‘Samar Balkan Main’ look at this cultural gap. So, there and this gap is not specifically language gap, it is a socio-cultural gap, your belief, so the English speakers looks at time in terms of money, so time is money, that is important. So, they place a lot of importance to money and we here in Indian context we say ‘Samar Balkan Main’ time is all powerful. So, the contexts are different, beliefs are different, value systems are different, and they are reflected in the language. So, while communicating cross-culturally, we have to be neutral, and we have to adhere to the language-specific cultural norms because it becomes a barrier, translating an idea from one culture and sharing it with other culture you have to meet the common ground otherwise, this can be a gap, an impediment, a barrier, metaphors for that matter are again problematic. Metaphors are frozen expressions but translating metaphors is a big challenge. Sometimes the inappropriate selection of words, inappropriate selection of sentences, misplaced tone, misplaced stress may create a lot of confusion and change in the meaning. And of course, the social use of language in an appropriate socio-cultural context. Let us say for that matter, mode of greeting or let us see the politeness norms in a culture, so the norms of politeness in Indian culture is different from norms of politeness in British culture for that matter, in American culture for that matter, most of the greetings are different, the patterns of socialization are different, the way we socialize, the way we start a conversation, the way we move on in a conversation, the way we interrupt, the way we intervene, the way we disagree, so the tone for that matter all these things are very sensitive when we communicate.  So, we have to be sensitive towards them and be particular and specific and sure that we are not mixing our cultural beliefs, values and things, and inappropriately translating that into other language and creating a lot of confusion and gap. So, language becomes a barrier if we are not able to understand, if you are not able to understand the socio-cultural context in which you are using it, if you are not able to have the proper selection of expressions and words according to the context in which you are going to use them, if you do not understand the audience with which you are communicating, so even if you are communicating in English it can create a lot of confusion, gap and barrier. Semantic barrier refers to the meaning part of it, the intended meaning. We need to understand for that matter, suppose somebody visits you, and you say why don't you sit? Now, structurally it is a question but if you look at the pragmatic aspect of it, meaning of it, it is actually an offer; you are offering a seat. So, there are lots of nuances in language that we need to pay attention to in order to communicate effectively.  Then the third category of barriers we can think of and talk about is socio-psychological barriers. So, when we say socio-psychological barriers, it is purely socio-cultural background of these communication partners that plays a very significant role. So, we all perceive things differently. We have our own world views and perceptions and such interpersonal differences and individuality do play a very significant role in exchange for messages and in effective communication. Social cultural differences in terms of values, beliefs, stereotypes, group norms, or biases and ethnocentrism. They all are very crucial and important. So, see we all have our biases; sometimes what is group norm? There are certain beliefs and practices that you continue with in order to remain the member of a group, a social group, we all have collective social biases towards individuals or groups, we all have stereotypes about people, about the caste, about the class. Look at for example, gender, gender is a marker, a very powerful marker, so your attitude towards gender does influence your communication pattern, your values, your beliefs, your stereotypes about gender, they do play a role in the pattern of your communication, and you become judgmental, it becomes a problem when we communicate, we have stereotypes about gender, gender related stereotypes, we have caste related stereotypes, we have class related stereotypes, we have region related stereotypes, we have religion related stereotypes, and remotely they all influence our communication patterns. There are certain expressions which are not considered appropriate in your public behavior, social context. We all have our individual biases, individual likings and disliking, at the same time collective biases, social biases. So, we need to work them out for effective communication, we need to work them out, we need to be balanced and neutral, and we can be effective communicator. But if you are not able to work out, if you are not able to work out your stereotypes, your biases, your ethnocentrism, then your judgments will be biased, you're encoding of the message will be biased. So, it is important to work them out, they all work as socio-psychological barrier, individually as well as collectively. Because we develop certain attitudes, we develop certain social behavior, in order to remain part of that particular social group, you have to subscribe to those social norms and behaviors. But in a cross-cultural context in which you communicate, all such things become a barrier, all such things create a lot of confusion and communication gap, so they become a barrier, and you have to work them out.  Moving on we have organizational barriers. It is interesting to see that we create rules, regulations, networks to facilitate communication, to control, to regulate but these regulations controlling mechanism, these rules they also turn out to be a barrier because the hierarchy, organization hierarchy for that matter creates a barrier, becomes problematic in free flow of information, the status of the speaker. And always remember your message is interpreted with relation to your location, your situation in a social space, so your status, your position in the organization, the hierarchical practices when we assert power, insistence on proper channel of communication in the organization. Sometimes we have our own priorities away from, apart from organizational priorities, our goals, our individual goals may not be aligned with organizational goals. Organizations may have rigidity in their policies because of the rules regulations and such regulations the regulatory measures you may have dissatisfaction, your attitude towards the seniors in the organization, the attitude of seniors towards the subordinates in the organization deficit of trust. So they all become barrier to effective communication free flow of exchanges.  So, these are the things that, these are the barriers or types of impediments which are there because of organizational structure, hierarchy, communication, pattern, networks and power distribution. And they become a barrier in communication, so we have to understand the limitations of these things and work them out. Otherwise, despite your best effort your message may not be communicated effectively, interpreted with the same intended meaning and content, there are possibilities of that, so you have to work them out.  And finally, we come to personal barriers and this is individual, and we all have such things in mind, in our dispositions, so we have to work them out, like we have perceptual differences, we all perceive things differently, we all have our own world views, and we see things according to that, we all have attitudes, different attitudes to our different things, sometimes inattention when we are not paying attention. Occupied mind, you may be occupied with other thoughts and communicating or premature evaluation sometimes we are desperate to communicate, we are desperate to speak, so we are not able to see things in totality, we evaluate situation prematurely and speak. We have this tendency of selective omissions. So, things that do not suit us we simply do not register, so you become selective in registering, selective in omitting things. We all filter information, we do not accept, we are not robots, we receive the information, we filter it, we understand it, we contextualize it, we interpret it. So, lots of filtering happens, and of course if the message or the content is demanding or beyond our capacity to receive and interpret, we lose a lot of fact and information.  So, there are certain personal things that we have to work it out, our skills, our promptness, our proactive approach in communication, attention, focusing on the message and the conversation, being patient, a good listener and do not evaluate things premature and our overall attitude and willingness to participate in communication act, they are all barriers, and we have to work them out to become effective communicator.  So, developing and maintaining a system of good communication is the primary job of us as an individual. And it largely depends on reciprocal understanding, mutual exchange of ideas, facts and information. So, we have to develop a shared understanding, we have to have shared meaning, and we need to customize the message in order to make sure that your message is received appropriately, interpreted appropriately and the intended meaning is communicated without any distortion and ambiguity.  So, what we can do? There are certain things that we have to keep in mind, two-way channel that means the communication must be participative in nature; you have to give space to the listener and audience, your audience, your receiver to participate in the process. Turn taking and turn giving, so, turn taking is important, equally important is turn giving. Receiving the feedback. Communication is all about developing connecting with the audience and developing a trust mutual trust, clarity of message, timing of the message, your consistency in the message, logical reasoned, well-reasoned and logical messages. Being positive, at least expressing positive outlook, periodical feedback, getting feedback from the audience, from the receiver that the receiver is receiving, remaining connected with the receiver, emphatic listening is very important; you have to be very good listener to be a very good communicator, most of the time we speak pre-measure.  So, you have to look at the things in totality, you have to evaluate things in a context with open mind and open heart that is called flexibility. And of course, last but not the least socio-cultural appropriateness. So, it is important to understand and have command on grammar; it is important to have command on the structure, it is important to have a wide range of vocabulary and words and expressions to use.  But we will talk about the next, in the next video we will talk about the context, so text is important but equally important is the context in which this text is exchanged, so message is exchanged, we communicate. So, who communicates what to whom, when, why and how, they together make your communication act effective and result oriented. So, I hope that you will keep these things in mind, and you will work them out. Always remember communication is an art and it requires a lot of practice. And communication is not about non-stop speaking, not about fluent speaking, not about appropriate accent and pronunciation; it is all about exchanging the meaningful content and ensuring the intended meaning to be communicated effectively, without any distortion and ambiguity. Because communication has a certain objective, there is a difference between gossip and communication. So, when we communicate there is a communication goal and all our acts should converge towards achieving that communication goal. So, this is for now, and we will continue our discussion about this context and about the appropriate of socio-cultural appropriation communication in our next class. Thank you very much.

title: Writing an Essay or a Research Report
text: English II – Professor Rajesh Kumar Department of Humanities and Social Sciences Indian Institute of Technology, Madras Welcome to the class, today, we are going to talk about writing.  We are going to talk about some specific tips, certain things to keep in mind when we write an essay or a research report.  In general, we are going to talk about writing, and then we will go to the specific details of what we must keep in mind when we are writing something.  Writing is an art, writing is a learnable skill in the process of language learning. Let me orient you with the skills that we have been talking about, we have talked about reading, speaking, writing and listening.  Out of these, speaking and listening are associated which is when we learn a language as a child, as a language as our first language or several languages at a time as a child as first language, we need to know that such a learning is automatic, such a learning is effortless.  In our efforts in learning language as a child, we do not need systematic instructions, we only need to hear things which is called receiving input from our society, from our immediate surroundings. And that input gets processed in mind with its available structure, which is part of the language acquisition device and in a miraculous way, the capacity to speak develops in us. Based on the findings of how that capacity develops, we have derived certain things to present in a particular order, keeping in mind those processes to learn a new language at a later stage. However, learning a new language at a later stage particularly after 15 years of age requires more effort, requires effort, requires systematic instruction, requires us to keep in mind what, how rules work and how they are derived from hearing, how human mind processes input.  So, we can learn a language, we can learn to speak a language at a later stage also.  So, in short, learning to speak and learning to hear, these two things go hand in hand, go together. In order to be able to speak a new language the precondition is listening. We must be in a position to hear what we want to speak.  That is heard the language that we are learning, this in a way works for first language acquisition as well.  And this is why under the premises of first language acquisition, we say that this capacity to develop normal, develop natural language effortlessly is in many ways restricted to a child born with normal abilities. Some children born with difficulties may have severe or mild difficulties in learning to speak.  That is a completely different field of study.  So, coming back, this is normal, natural and learning to speak at early stage or at a later stage, go hand in hand with learning to listen.  Listening as part of learning to speak, from the perspective of the use of language, from learning, pragmatic constraints, pragmatic as part of pragmatic competence in terms of what to speak, what not to speak, more importantly, when to speak and when not to speak. These are parts of softer skills that we acquire as part of normal etiquette, or some kind of intelligence, intelligent behavior in communication.  At times, we say a lot by not saying anything as well. People understand our intentions underlying our speaking to a great deal with the movements of our body parts, which is known as body language. So, we keep conveying a lot of things without speaking as well. So, that is also part of another kind of learning. And these are important aspects of learning to communicate.  Communication, in its totality, is not just about what we speak.  And the rules, underlying what we speak, rules underlying what we see is crucial for accuracy and formulating your sentence, your expression accurately, because it is a strong understanding and rule that without accuracy, we do not sound effective. Without accuracy, we are not taken serious LY.  So, if we want someone to take what we speak seriously, we need to speak with accuracy flawlessly, and that comes through that builds the confidence that comes through confidence and that builds confidence in speaking. And once you are, you trust yourself on your accuracy, you can formulate your ideas, you can formulate what you want to say with more ease and effectiveness for others. So, these are all parts of communications.  Another part of communication which we are concerned with today is writing. We communicate a lot of things in writing. And therefore, writing is a skill to o, it is very different kinds of skill from speaking in the sense that it is learnable, and it can be learned only by efforts. Writing is not an innate capacity for us to acquire. It is possible and there are millions of people across the world who speak flawlessly. But they do not write because they did not learn to write their either it is, mostly that comes from the cases of first language.  So, whatever language we speak as our first language Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Aria, Bangle, Assumes, whatever we speak it is possible that millions of speakers of those languages do not know how to write because they did not, they never learned writing those things. As part of learning a second language like English, it is rare. It is rare and mostly uncommon, that a person can speak but cannot write because the moment we start learning a second language at a later stage, writing precedes speaking.  Learning to write and subsequently learning to read perceived learning to speak.  So, I am only trying to make the point that learning to write is a skill that we need to put efforts in. And it is a learnable skill number 1, number 2, so that is basic writing of scripts, alphabet and combining them together and words and spellings and so on. When we are, when we cross that stage, and we want to communicate through writing, this is where what we are going to talk today makes a difference.  At that stage, what we need to keep in mind as one of the most fundamental roles is when we communicate through writing, we are not there to speak those things. That is, reader on the other side is going to understand and read only what is written on the piece of paper. So, communication in writing is different from communication in speaking, we do not get a chance to repeat ourselves, we do not get a chance to explain ourselves, we do not get a chance to describe things once we have finished writing.  So, writing is a skill, it is an art and it is learnable. And it is different from speaking. However, it is an important component of communication. So, so many things can make our writing effective. And we need to keep some of these things in mind as generic advice, as tips, and we can improve on it. More importantly, writing on a regular basis can improve writing itself. Writing is also a matter of habit formation.  So, I suggest here that you do keep writing something on daily basis, writing is very much self-indulgent.  You need to invest yourself and indulge yourself in the process. It gives you relief from many things that might be going on simultaneously in your mind. It gives you relief from your immediate environment because it captures your attention and helps you focus on one point.  In some ways, if we can borrow the metaphor, writing is like yoga. And that is the level which is required for literary writing, or creative writing, or to make yourself a very sound writer. We need to write so many things. Sometimes we just need to write a letter, sometimes we just need to write a short essay, a short paragraph, a short description, a short report, and so on. All these things require different kinds of skills.  So it is, it is not possible for us to talk about all kinds of writing, but I wanted to discuss this with you in terms of simpler things that we can always keep in mind, nonetheless, what we need to write, and also we needed to know what we, what is writing all about. So, please keep in mind writing is like yoga. Writing helps you focus. We cannot write properly without focus, without forgetting immediate environment and without a lot of preparations.  You need to think, ideate, stop, meditate a lot before you can put things in writing. With the help of computers, it is much easier that you can rearrange your sentences without deleting much, without putting in much effort. Whatever works for you, whether writing on a computer or a tab or a phone or a notebook, do write because that is prerequisite.  However, if you can let yourself write on a piece of paper this may sound old-fashioned, but this is going to help you a great deal in writing on computer also.  It will not show up like speaking, when you are learning to speak a language. First, it takes a lot of time to reach the point where you are confident about your sentences, your pronunciation, where you feel you are making a meaningful discourse and conversation, it takes time.  Similarly, writing a full page without being left around, in the sense that without being disconnected in your ideas takes time. But if you write on a piece of paper, that is writing in a notebook is undoubtedly more helpful than writing on a computer screen. Nonetheless, what is more important is writing per se.  So, having said this much, let me just say a few more things about what we need to keep in mind. So, as I said, while thinking about it, it requires you to go through your ideas multiple times.  And at that stage, it might, it looks unorganized, disorganized, your ideas may appear scattered in pieces, in terms of information. And sometimes it might be confusing also. All these things could appear on the piece of paper as well.  So, thinking through a point clearly reflects on the piece of paper, as well. So, this is the exercise that we need to do in the background of writing.  Of course, it requires grammar. That is accuracy. If you are writing on a machine that is computer, you have a lot of options. And there are a lot of other helpful pieces of software that can help you write your sentences.  But if you are writing on a piece of paper, all these things happen cognitively. And I repeat one more time, you start writing on a piece of paper, give yourself 90 days. And then compare your writing at the ninetieth day from the from your own writing on the first day, you will be surprised to the extent that you want to recognize your own writing.  I am not speaking to professional creative writers. I am speaking to the people who are in the process of learning to write, who are hesitant writing, all of us get hesitant because writing is creating record, creating a document, writing is some point from where we do not go back. So, we hesitate in writing. This is why some people may keep their writing personal. And writing is also, a large part of writing is personal.  We are not trying to make a distinction between personal and public writing.  But you need to go through a lot of efforts at your personal level to make your writing public where people make sense out of your writing. So, this requires a lot of effort. And I am, at that stage I am telling you that you will not be able to recognize your own writing after 3 months from the time you started. Compare the two for yourself, this is a nice kind of exercise or a gift that you can allow yourself to do. So, your grammatical accuracy will also go up. If you make mistakes, leave it, but when you compare it after 3 months, you say you can see that your grammatical mistakes have disappeared. It happens let me stop here because we want to talk about a few more things about writing. Sentence structure, punctuation s, that is where to put a full stop, where to put a comma, where to put a semicolon, you will need to pay attention to these things as well. And therefore, your attention in reading something carefully will have direct impact on what you are going to write. All these subconscious processing is going to yield result for that as well.  So, you are developing your own vocabulary, your sentence structure and knowledge you gain about a subject and the basic writing skills, all of them are going to get imported from your time that you invest in reading something.  So, when you move from there, you need to, so there are some steps that you need to follow and end it helps. So, to give you a writing structure, you need to have clarity about your concept that you are going to write.  Suppose, you are writing an official letter, you need to have clear points that these are the things that you are going to write and in a particular order for particular event. So, it is like preparation.  So, you know, it is a very simple, and sometimes it is intuitive also. Like we prepare for travel. When we pack our bags, the things that we need later, we put them at the bottom, and something that we need on the way or immediately after arriving, we might put them on the top. It is that type of preparation, which we need to apply in writing. So, you need to outline things in order to reduce complexity.  You may need to anticipate the questions the reader might have after reading, after writing something at the time of conceptualizing the point, or after reading your own writing, you need to anticipate what your readers, what questions your readers may come up with. And if you can sort them out in your writing that is an effort in making your writing impactful.  In this process, you also need to keep in mind that you do not overdo something, you do not explain it to the extent that it does not remain challenging to the readers, it is a very tough task. Not to underestimate the emotional intelligence or emotional quotient of your readers at the same time, not to leave things for too much of imaginations of the reader, striking a balance between the two is a tough task. We reached that point later. But these things are helpful.  We need to be a little bit careful about using long sentences with too many post positional phrases. As you know, post positional phrases are adjuncts we do not need to give, we do not need to overload our sentences. We do see the uses of subordinate clauses a lot in writing, but we need to be little careful about that.  In writing, we are completely going to remove filler words and phrases the way we use them while speaking, like ah, umm, I think so, I did not know, I do not know, these kinds of, there are a lot of filler phrases. I hope it is clear. There are a lot of things that we do, that we use in spoken language which we do not need to bring in writing, in that sense also writing is very different exercise. So, basically you will need to practice getting to that point.  It helps to know, what is the type of our writing, what are we, what is our goal? Who is our intended audience? If that is in mind, it becomes very helpful. So, sometimes we keep, we write about, our essay could be argumentative type. It is an or an admission type or a persuasive type or a comparison, we are trying to write a comparison or contrast. It could be a personal essay in terms of a memoir or a diary or expository in nature.  So, each one of them will have their own specific things, specific requirements. And once you go into the details of that, you can learn more about them, what clarity and accuracy are the foundations of these things.  However, please keep in mind as footnote, you do not need to strive for clarity and accuracy right on the first day. Rather, clarity and accuracy comes through writing over a long period of time.  So, we need to decide, if we keep in mind the kind of writing we have to do that will give you lot of clarity in terms of thinking through your topic. And thinking through your topic will also require you to look at your topic. If you have to make a presentation around that you need to research that topic carefully. You will need to be dependent on particular type of style or certain specific vocabulary of that type of writing.  Sometimes you need to just make a sort her outline of what you want to write before you go into the details of developing your writing. And then when you finally write, you finally have a piece of writing do make sure that you edit your writing, if you are doing it on computer, it is very simple to edit it through spell-check or multiple types of checks.  Even when you are writing on a piece of paper, and you have to dispatch it to somebody, you can wait if it is for yourself, but if you have to dispatch your writing to somebody, do make sure that it is you make it a habit that you reread, edit, and then send it to somebody.  Particularly this becomes in principle a better practice, if we are writing an email, we must reread our sentences in email before hitting the send button. Because once you have sent it, there is nothing to undo. So, rereading is the process of editing and that is a good practice for any kind of writing.  When we prepare a research report, research report is very specific thing because research has to proceed before we put it in the form of a report.  So, the first thing about a research report is to organize it in a particular order that we state the research problem, we describe the problem, and then we describe the method, which is the steps that we have taken in order to do research, then we need to come to the body where we need to present evidence, an argument in support of the evidence that have come. And finally, we write a conclusion that is what are the conclusive points derived out of the research in the whole process. So, this is why it is called a report the whole thing has happened, we just need to put them in that order in writing. Again, it might require certain specific vocabulary depending on the type of research, but it is these are some of the steps.  So, if all research is academic in nature, so we need to demonstrate familiarity with the topics as well, which is sometimes called literature survey or literature review, we need to present the entire wealth or bulk of survey, bulk of familiarity with the literature, which has helped you sharpen up your question. See, the key point in a research report is the research question. And it is imperative for writing a research report to show the trajectory through which you have reached the question, the point.  These things are helpful in any kind of writing as well, but particularly for research.  Now, if you, since I have mentioned the term research several times, any research is about a systematic study, a systematic process, research in other word means a systematic process. And a systematic process requires three different stage, systematic can also be called scientific, anything that is systematic is scientific.  So, it requires three different stages. One is observation, stage of observation, when we first observe something. Then comes the stage of description that is describing what we observe. And third is explaining what we have observed and described.  So, these are three steps and in that order, because if you look backward, it is tough to explain anything, or we can go to the extent of saying it is impossible to explain anything unless we have described it for ourselves. And how do we describe something if we have not observed carefully. So, these are the steps in the background for research and keeping them in mind also helps us put them in the form of a report.  So, again, keep in mind, so, you could be, you could have different kinds of research reports. So, and once we move ahead, we, in order to describe we make, we need to make notes. In order to write a final report also, we need to go back and consult our notes because in this entire process, it is impossible to remember everything.  And then we need to give them a shape of organization and that is an important step in designing any report.  Keeping an outline in mind, and how we introduce a topic, what is going to be the body and how we reached to the conclusion are par ts of the steps that I have just described to you. And finally, you do allow yourself to go through the checklist of this for writing a report. Because a report is going to, the way you present your report is going to present your entire work to others, the better the report the better you have a possibility to convince others.  I conclude by saying the lot of scientists, a lot of writers, a lot of work can only be conveyed through writing, you can convince people only through good writing. So, good piece of writing and organized in an organized fashion can only be impressive and impactful. In the process of writing impressive does not mean selecting too many adjectives or too many adverbs. In fact, we should avoid using too many adjectives. We should avoid writing too many passive sentences and impressive and impactful writing is contingent and dependent on our capacity, our ability to organize it properly in our mind.  So, striking a balance through this can allow you to explain, to present your work through writing to others in your absence, because when we write, we keep in mind that for the reader, we are only present in the form of our words, in the form of that report, and we do not have a chance there to add or delete anything from there.  So, one more time writing is a learnable skill, important part, requires a lot of practice and writing repeatedly over a long period of time can allow us to become impressive. Nobody becomes perfect, right in the beginning, right in their few attempts. So if it takes time, it is not abnormal. Please allow yourself time, keeping these things in mind.  More importantly, and the last point, which I repeat, where I repeat myself, please continue writing. Indulge yourself in writing. You will get there. Thank you very much for listening. We look forward to hearing from you, your questions, comments on these topics, these things and until we meet next time, take care.

title: Metaphors
text: English – II Advanced English Professor. Rajesh Kumar Department of Humanities and Social Sciences Indian Institute of Technology, Madras Metaphor Welcome to the class. Today, we are going to talk about metaphors. I am sure you have heard this word, metaphor, as the word is itself a metaphor. We will talk about it. Are related to meaning of a sentence. Metaphor works in the area of making meaning in conversation in the use of languages. When we learn language, particularly a new language at a later stage in our life, that is, after 15 years of our age, we need to put in harder efforts to understand metaphors related to that target language.  The reason is very simple, metaphors are usually culturally grounded. Metaphors in general are words or phrases that do not have direct or literal meaning. They sometimes compare one situation, one thing with the other, they are indirect ways of saying several things. We do not want to say so many things at times, and in such situations, in such context we use metaphorical expressions.  We are going to look at several examples of that, but before we do, it is important for you to know that the discussion here is not about memorizing metaphors in English. The discussion here is to understand the context in which metaphors is used, metaphor, a metaphor is used and how and under what circumstances we use metaphors.  As I mentioned to you, metaphors are related to meaning. There are two parts of a sentence, one is the structure, the other is the meaning. Sometimes it is argued that these two are separate parts. True, for the study of languages or the study of the structure of language, we can separate meaning from the structural analysis of language. However, for the purpose of learning a language, for the purpose of making sense of language, it is not fair to separate meaning from the structure. Therefore, it will be relevant for us to see how metaphors are culturally embedded, and it is structurally embedded as well.  We are going to see that metaphors are words, phrases, and they occur, they can occur at various different grammatical positions like object positions like adjunct position, and so on. In short, metaphors are pragmatic in nature, metaphors put us at a different cognitive stage, and we need to be smarter and sensitive to understand metaphors because sometimes it may ask us to read in between the lines. Metaphors are non-serious ways of saying serious things. Hence, understanding uses of metaphor is an important aspect of learning a new language. Let us move and see, start and see some examples.  So, let us look at these examples. Here are a few sentences like ‘she flew past me on her bicycle’. ‘Turing was the father of the modern computer’. ‘He gave me a cold look’. The bold, the phrases in bold are examples of metaphors. And here you can see that they are, they are not used in its literal meaning, they do not have, these words do not have their literal meaning. Meaning, when we say ‘flew past me’, ‘Turing was the father of modern computers’, ‘Father’ literally has a different meaning. And when we use here, ‘father’ in terms of modern computers, we mean he was the first few initial scientists working on computers. ‘He gave me a cold look’. You can see here, cold is being used as an adjective for the noun, look. How can a look be cold? It has a different meaning. What we intend this to mean is not the literal meaning of cold look. It means, he was he gave me, he did not display warmth, he did not display welcoming approach, welcoming attitude. So, these are the meanings of, this is the meaning of metaphor.  So, look at this, we could also say ‘he gave me a cold look’. In place of that, we can say, ‘he was not displaying warmth when he saw me’, but instead we are saying he gave me a cold look. The purpose is simple: that sometimes the use of metaphors says a lot more than we want to say, and this is the key factor. Hence, we could say ‘Turing was one of the first few scientists who worked on computers’, but this is another way of saying, ‘Turing was the father of modern computers’.  So, a metaphor is sometimes a comparison. When we use a word or a phrase as a metaphor, it does not carry literal meaning. These are the important things that I have just discussed with you. So, if when we say, ‘fly past’, she flies past on a bicycle or a car it is not literally flying through the air, but speed of the movement reminds you of a plane or a bird. So, only planes do fly past. So, when you say ‘she flies’, ‘she flew past me’. What was the example here? ‘She flew past me on her bicycle’. So it means, she was so fast, it was like a plane moving.  So, how does metaphor work? So, a metaphor contains an idea. This is the connection or, this is the connection or similarity between the literal meaning and metaphorical meaning, meaning when we use a metaphor, there is a connection. There may or may not be a connection between a literal meaning and the metaphorical meaning that we desire to get. Sometimes, we can use the same idea through different kinds of metaphors, through the different kinds of phrases. And so, one metaphor may not have just one idea.  For example, when we talk about illness, we often use the phrase whose literal meanings are to do with fighting wars. So, look at this, ‘a good diet will help you fight disease’. So, when we use the word ‘fight’ it is not an actual fight, it is fight with the disease so it is used in a metaphorical sense. ‘The virus attacks the immune system’. So, here ‘attack’ in the context of virus again, attack is a war expression. ‘Jean died on Saturday after a long battle with cancer’. So here again, battle with a disease. So, in the context of diseases, we use certain times like metaphors, which are close in the meaning.  So, we understand metaphors, and there is another term that is used is called idioms, but there is a difference between the two. An idiom is an expression where the derived meaning is different from the literal meaning of individual words. So, the literal, the use of words that we have for idioms, we are going to have a completely different meaning. So, the meaning of idioms is not the total of the meaning of words used for idiom.  However, a metaphor is an analogy between two objects or ideas that are conveyed by comparing two unrelated objects. So, we are going to look at the examples of that. So, when we say ‘this exam was a piece of cake’. So, this is an idiom, which can be used in a metaphorical sense, but it is an idiom. Because ‘piece of cake’, the total meaning of the word has nothing to do with the intended meaning that we want to get whereas, metaphor is an example. So when we say ‘babies are monkeys’. What we mean, what we mean, we do not mean literally, but there is a comparison between the two objects, so ‘monkeys’ are used as metaphors depicting babies for their naughty behavior or childlike behavior, we can use these terms. And we in that context, we say we can use these metaphors. So, a metaphor is a figurative expression, which compares two unrelated or related objects, without using the term ‘as’ or ‘like’.  So, let us look at the examples of some of these things in greater details with their meanings. And then we try to develop the context out of which, which will be helpful for us. So, ‘life is not black and white’. Here, the term black and white is used to highlight the ambiguous nature of life, uncertain, uncertainties of life. ‘His soul is black’: we use the term black to describe darkness or insensitive nature.  ‘He carries the weight of the world on his shoulders’. Huge amount of trouble emphasized by the weight of the world. So, when somebody is in a lot of trouble and looks very stressed, we can use this metaphor. ‘The police officer was digging up details about the suspect’: here digging up does not have its literal meaning, but trying to find out leads in the police investigation is the meaning of that.  ‘His irresponsible behavior made his health turn south’. Now ‘irresponsible behavior means his health turned south’, ‘turn south’ is a metaphor, and ‘turn south’ means that it worsened, became bad, worse. So, ‘wind screamed in his face while he was riding the bike’. Again, ‘scream’ simply means it is furious blowing. ‘Go for a walk, or you will become a couch potato’. Now this is an idiom, which is used in a metaphorical sense. This is used when, if you do not move the chances are becoming bulgy, like a potato if you do not move yourself. ‘Her heart of stone was the result of the previous unfortunate events in her life’. ‘Heart of stone’ meaning in a sense symbolizes a stone, it is emphasizing the lack of empathy or lack of sensitivity.  ‘Her mom warned her about the monsters in the world’ here again, ‘monster’ is used as metaphor for bad wicked people. ‘See the world from a different lens’: ‘different lens’ indicates or denotes different perspective. ‘He is an elderly; he is an early bird’. ‘Early bird’ is used for birds. Birds start their day too early. So, ‘early birds’ are used for people who wake up too early or arrive early to an event or a place of work or anything of that side.  ‘Life is no bed of roses’: ‘bed of roses’ is a very commonly used phrase. ‘Bed of roses’, where roses symbolizes, comfort, peace and ‘bed of roses’ is a greater sense of peace and comfort. We know life is not a bed of roses. So, it is filled of hardship and sacrifice that we have to do, and in such context, we use such expressions. ‘I will make sure she pays for her doings’: here, paying is used in a metaphorical way of, in a way of fixing so melody, so that you have to pay for what you did. ‘I am the master of my sea’. ‘Master of my sea’ is another expression, which emphasizes the fact that the person is the master of his own world. So, master is an important thing. A master of sea means master of your own world or own fate. ‘She wears different hats to earn a livelihood’. ‘Wearing different hats’ mean working for different identities or different jobs for earning a living.  ‘The good news about the profit made lifted his spirit’: ‘lifting the spirit’ is felt carefree, feel good, all of a sudden. ‘Taxes are minefield for people who are careless’: ‘minefield’ is used to denote the presence of dangerous consequences and problems. So, dangerous consequences. What happens in minefields if you are not careful, you can land into trouble simply tax is being compared with minefields. So, it is a very clear example of a metaphor. ‘She soon realized that she had been taken for a ride’: ‘being taken for a ride’ means that she has been tricked, she has been misled, misguided.  ‘She was a cheater in the race’, meaning the here, cheetah symbolizes speed. S o, when you run so fast, you can be called a cheetah. ‘You will be left in the dust’. Now again, it implies leaving being left far behind in such, in certain satiation.  ‘The professor was a guiding light on him’: ‘guiding light’ was a guiding light on him. ‘Guiding light’ means the professor is being compared with a light to help him pave the way easily.  So, when you show the light some, to somebody, it is called guiding being a guiding light, and you can see the meaning from here. ‘The curtains of life fell’: ‘the curtains’, falling curtain is compared with that so that the fallen denoting the person's life is over. So, falling, the curtain it is, this metaphor is coming from the field of drama, which symbolizes the end of life.  ‘Life is a maze’ it means, life is being said to have its own navigation, as you move ahead with the supplies at every turn. So, maze talks about a lot of things, which means, which symbolizes uncertainty. ‘There is a rat among us’: here, ‘rat’ is being ING used as metaphor. It is a sneaky animal, so you can guess the meaning. So, in a group, if somebody leaks the secret it is, and which leads to betrayal, in such situations, people use this metaphor that ‘there is a rat among us’.  ‘Her heart sank on hearing the terrible’. So, sinking of heart means, slipping into deep sorrow or deep, it emphasizes sorrow, sorrow. So, when we sink in, when heart sinks, it does not sink for any happiness, it sinks only for sorrow. ‘Laughter is the best medicine’: ‘best medicine’ here is being compared, laughter is compared with the best medicine in the sense that it has good impact. It helps recover.  So, ‘India's culture is a salad bowl’. Sometimes it can be also said as a ‘melting pot’. These are the metaphors, which are used for what happens in a salad bowl. You do not have just one thing, you have onion, cucumber, tomatoes and all kinds of stuff mixed together. So, when multiple things are together that is the meaning here, that is the meaning we want to derive. So, you can imagine India's culture and its multiplicity is being referred to as a salad bowl or a melting pot.  A melting pot has little different meaning. It means they melt together to become something else. So, if you, what do you do in melting pot? You put different things and mix them.  Sometimes they can retain their identity, sometimes they might lose. But anyway, it is a melting, it means the same thing.  ‘His heart was made of gold’: here, ‘gold’ and heart is being compared, so gold is a valuable entity, good, it symbolizes good. So you can guess the meaning that heart being compared with gold is a symbol of abundance and generosity. So, like I mentioned before, we do use metaphors in informal contexts in, at any part of the sentence, but it has special meaning.  And sometimes people use metaphors in special context to make things look formal.
