So, this is what we understand by developing effective listening and the myth that listening is a passive exercise is a misnomer and not appropriate. Listening is a very active exercise, and we need to be actively engaged with the listener, the oral text and most importantly, it does not come in a flash easily with you, we need to have a lot of practice we need to have a lot of exposure to different accents, different styles, different speakers, native speakers, non-native speakers.  We need to be exposed to a variety of oral texts that will help us develop our listening skills, fine-tune our interpretation, and it will make you a very productive speaker by being a good listener or patient listener. Thank you very much.

title: Developing Speaking Skills in English
text: English 2 Dr Om Prakash Guest Faculty, Humanities and Social Sciences Indian Institute Technology Chennai Welcome to class; in continuation with our fundamentals of communication, communication skills, we will focus today on one of the linguistic skills, very importantly linguistic skills, that is speaking skills. It is also a very active skill, productive skill, so people call it we buy different names, productive skills, active skills, but listening, speaking, is essentially a very productive and effective skill.  When you speak, when you open your mouth, the utterances, the sentences, the words that you speak, they tell a lot about you, so we have to be very particular, specifically in our professional domain, because lots of things are interpreted out of it, sometimes intended messages, sometimes something which is unintentional, it is also, interpreted with the tone, with the speed, with the delivery, with the manner in which you deliver.  So, we have to be a little prepared in our professional domains when we speak; we need to speak effectively. So, what do you say is very important? But equally important is how you say it, and speaking in public or speaking to different people in an official setting, in a professional setting, can be made easy if we locate and identify a few shortcomings in our delivery.  And there is no; there is no universal list that talks about the shortcomings of in speaking, because this is a very personalized, individual skill. So, we all speak differently. But there are certain universal things that must be present. When you speak, like the intent, the content, the format, the mode, the tone, fluency.  So, we have to be a little careful about all these things and speaking can be made easy and effective. So do not worry about the speed. Do not worry about the accent, do not worry about high-frequency words or simple sentences; they are required, and we can overcome a few problems that we have. So, let us first understand what problems do we have in speaking English. English is not your mother tongue, and we are not a native speaker of English; English is our second language. To some people, it is a third language.  We learn English in a formal setting, we do not use English in our everyday life, in most of the situations, English is the language of higher education. So in average, formal settings, we have English present, and we are multilingual by nature; we all come from a different linguistic background that also interferes with your performance in English.  So, there are certain problems, and what I have done, I have listed them out of my experience with different students in the class and people who use English in the professional domain. So, there are certain problems we all are aware of.  I will just underline a list of things that may happen; not necessarily all of these are present with you; you all have the same problem. Some of them may be a problem area for you. So, this list is just to understand those problem areas, identify those problem areas and work on them and the first thing and the most important thing is anxiety and believe me, it is quite natural. You do not have to be worried about it.  We all have anxiety when we speak in a formally learned language called English. That is not our natural expression does not come through this language. So we all have this specific anxiety about speaking English. So, you might have seen people, who speak in normal speech, normal variation with normal tempo at a normal speed, who look very relaxed, when they use their mother tongue or the even non-English language, any non-English language which they have learned and used as a bilingual.  But, the moment you start speaking English we get a kind of stress on the face, stress, unnecessary stress comes in, you become cautious, you become, it becomes obvious that you are making an effort, anxiety and nervousness maybe they are with some people not every one of you, but some people may have this nervousness and anxiety before speaking English, so speaking become challenging for them, it leads to lack of confidence because the moment you are nervous, and you have anxiety, then your confidence is shaken up.  You become overcautious. You are dominated by a tendency of hypercorrection. So, we had this continuous fear of mistakes, continuous fear of mistake because you do not appear natural, you become effortful, you are making efforts. So, that leads to nervousness, that amounts to anxiety that shakes up your confidence, you become hyper corrective.  So, you will start correcting even if it is not required. So relax, you do not have to worry, it is very natural, and it happens with most of us. Then, another problem is that we find the ideas are scattered because the thought process does not seem consistent and continuous. So, we have to make a lot of effort to collect our ideas; we are continuously haunted by this fear of mistake, sometimes lack of preparation on the content also leads you to that.  Then, if you do not have good control on the content or if you lack appropriate linguistic skills, you have inappropriate communication strategies; most of us, when we speak English, we speak in monotone. So, there is no animation in the voice, no variation in the voice; our body becomes stiff and rigid. So, this natural flow and flexibility is missing and frequent distractions because you are so alert and so concentrated that sometimes we lose control, and sometimes you are distracted because of various emotions we are challenged with.  So, these are certain challenges, and why they happen because you are not speaking in your mother tongue; you do not have a natural flair. This is not your native language. You have not learned this language in an informal setting. Natural expression or spontaneity is missing. So, lots of reasons and lots of challenges, I have just listed a few.  We need to under identify and understand where do I need to work on. On my anxiety part, and let me tell you, they are all integrated and related. They are not independent problems because improvement in one will fit into the other. So, if you become confident, suddenly you find that your anxiety and nervousness is gone, you are confident, and the moment you become confident, spontaneity and fluency automatically follow.  If you have control on the content you are going to speak, you are going to talk about, you will have confidence. So, these are all interrelated. They are not independent; they are interdependent. So, improvement in one area helps you develop in other area and this is how we develop it overall.  It can be made easy it is not difficult. A few home works that we need to do before talking in public or before making a presentation, or before interacting formally, we need to make some home works, we need to do some homework, make some preparations, and that is pre-speech event preparations. So, first and foremost, you should know your audience.  Whom are you talking to? In order to become an effective speaker, you need to understand your audience; then, you need to prepare on what you are going to talk about. So, your topic, theme, you must be familiar, and you should prepare on that and that will help you develop control on the contents.  Then, collect all required information, if possible, and sometimes you may not have time to do so, because you have to do make a speech or interact in a group, hold up office meeting quickly. But again, the smartness is that you need to collect some information before you start talking, and for that, you need to be familiar with the theme and develop your own opinion about it.  So, it is a complex process; it helps you develop confidence, control over the content, then you have to organize the information you have, in the synchronic order and then how to introduce an idea, introduction of your idea must be effective and when you elaborate it because you need to draw the attention of your audience while introducing the idea, and then you can elaborate and discuss and continue.  The arguments that you put forward or the qualifying sentences that you utter after the introduction, they must be logical, coherent and meaningful. You should avoid unnecessary repetitions. If you need to repeat paraphrase it, emphasize on the portions what you feel important. Pauses work wonders; pauses are important. You have to take a pause intermittently, but not unnecessarily.  Stretching a pause may bore your audience, may distract your audience. But pauses are important before we, suppose you are going to introduce a very important idea, a little pause before that will suddenly draw the attention of your audience to what you are going to speak, allow them to anticipate what is coming, a little pause works wonder when you changed the idea.  So, these are certain tips we need to keep in mind. So, when we say effective speaking, what does it imply? So, speaking intelligibly. So, what you speak must be easy for others to comprehend; that is the first condition. Be intelligible. Then speaking fluently, and fluent speaking does not mean speaking without a break or speaking without a pause or speaking at a very high speed, no.  Fluency refers to the continuity of idea and continuity of utterances and sentences. So, it should not be interruption at the content level, at the format level. So, language must be in a flow, utterances must be in a singular flow, single flow and there must be continuity in the idea, progressive continuity, continuously progressive and idea is continuous and progresses to a certain direction as you intended. But if it puts on, puts a lot of cognitive load on your audience, then it can be problematic. So, it has to be intelligible and fluent, and it comes when you are confident while speaking. So, you should sound confident, you should look confident, and you should be confident, and you can be confident, you can sound confident, and you can look confident only when you are well-prepared.  So, preparation is very important. Paraphrasing is a signal of your confidence and control. So, only those speakers, paraphrase, who have control on the content and who have confidence, because you might have seen people are always in a hurry to finish what they want to say and why it happens. It happens because they are scared of losing it midway.  So, you need to be confident, and you should not appear in a hurry to finish what you want to say. It should be finished within time, no doubt about it. But that you should not be desperate to finish. So, paraphrasing signals confidence of the speaker, and also it implies that the speaker is considerate in engaging the audience and communicating the content effectively, the paraphrasing is a very positive thing because it makes the understanding easy for your audience, if they are not able to follow you what you say. Then you should also engage people and always remember, even if you are making a presentation of in office or official presentation, you should invite questions, you should invite feedbacks intermittently and that keeps your audience engaged at the same time, you can gauge whether they are able to follow you effectively or not or have you delivered your message effectively or not.  So, asking for feedback and how can you do that by just asking a simple question based on what you said or inviting a suggestion or underline an opinion. So, you can do it in multiple ways, but engage your audience when you speak. Then sound interactive skills, you might have seen people get agitated; they start responding in a very agitated manner.  No, you need to be calm, composed, relaxed, and you need to, you need to give this, give this impression that you are in control. You are poised; you are calm and in control. So, you have to look composed, you do not have to sound disparate, scared or irritated or agitated. Like you could that leaves a very bad impression and negative impression on your audience and when you invite questions, when you invite suggestions, respond to them. It has to be two-way.  Moving on. So, in effective speaking, what linguistic skills are required. Always remember vocabulary, grammar and pronunciation. These three things are very important —pronunciation, vocabulary and grammar. So, you have to have fairly good command on pronunciation; you should utter sounds clearly as I told you, you do not have to sound like anyone, any other person or native speaker or an American speaker, a native speaker, a British native speaker not at all.  If you have an understanding of sounds of English and if you minimize the interference of your mother tongue to a little extent and if you are able to pick up a neutralized accent, that is sufficient for you. Then, in order to express what you are saying, in order to express what yo u intend to say, you need to have a fairly good command on a wide range of vocabulary, and that comes with so many exercises and practices that you enhance your input language input.  So, require a lot of input in terms of words and when you start using these words, they become part of your verbal repertoire; you do not have to put a lot of effort to bring in, you can easily recall them. So, good command on vocabulary and grammar. You do not need to be a grammarian, but you should have fundamental functional understanding of grammar, English sentences.  That will help you in speaking effectively, then appropriately in handling a range of topics, the range of contexts, selecting appropriate expressions, words and structures, because always remember, we cannot replace any word with any word; every word has a semantic matrix, a shade we need to understand.  For example, suppose you say incident, accident, disaster, calamity, pandemic for that matter, now we have catastrophic for that matter. So, all these words denote similar kind of semantic content, but incident cannot be replaced with accident, accident cannot be replaced with disaster, disaster cannot be replaced with catastrophe, catastrophe cannot be replaced with pandemic.  So, like sink, drown and capsize, sink drawn and capsize. So, any word is not a replacement of another word; every word has got a particular context and a semantic matrix. For example, we cannot say something like, we can say strong coffee, we can say sharp knife, we can say a sharp mind, we can say intelligent mind, but can we say intelligent knife, not at all.  So, sharp with mind you can have sharp, sharp mind, intelligent mind, but with knife I cannot have intelligent knife, I can have strong man, I can have a powerful man, I can have a strong woman, a powerful woman that is fine, I can say strong coffee, but can I say powerful coffee, no. So, powerful and strong cannot be replaced by each other.  So, we need to understand the word and the context in which they are used, so the word and the use, then only you will be to express select semantically, effective lexicon or word, for a particular purpose. Then you need to be good at understanding connectors, sentence connectors. So, how we can connect multiple sentences in speech, where to put stress, what are the linking devices, because in writing it is obvious you can see, but in speaking, you will have a lot of repetitions, a lot of overlaps.  We need to connect ideas, and while connecting ideas, you need to have longer sentences so in that case, you need some linking devices, and, if, whether, that, you need to understand elision and assimilation, cohesion. How to put structures in a cohesive manner, in a logical order? How to construct your ideas logically and put them in sentences? How to have coherent sentences, lucid sentences? So, we need to understand them, elision, intonation, assimilation, speaker, when the speaker speaks and if you have a same sound in the word ending position and word beginning position.  So, let us say bad, b-a-d and doll, d-o -l-l, The. So, the sound The is the ending sound or the first word and The is the beginning sound or the second word.  So, when you are speaking separately, two individual words sound two different words, but we uses these two different words in a connective speech, they assimilate, so we say, bad doll, bad doll, bad doll, we do not say badder doll, d twice, we say bad doll, fast train, fast, Ta is the last word, train Ta is the first word of the second word, but when you speak together, we do not say faster train, we say strain. So, one Ta is assimilated, and they become one sound. So, we need to understand all of these factors.  Now, there are certain interactive skills we need to develop to become a good speaker, like fluency we have been talking about, speaking at natural speed, linking and pausing naturally. So, when you stop, to breathe or to collect your idea, you have to be smart enough to play with this pause, and that is why elevation in the voice is required, you can play with this pause, to get some breather and also time to collect your idea.  You have to be smart in that, and it will come to you gradually with practice. In the act of paraphrasing, you need to develop this act of paraphrasing, speaking about the same idea in different ways, in different manners, so that your audience understands it better without any effort. You have to have alternate explanations if required. You have to substantiate what we are saying with examples. Allow people to ask questions and feedback.  So very quickly, we need to understand the significance of pronunciation and vocabulary in good speaking. How to become a good speaker? You have to have a fairly good amount of control on pronunciation. As I told you, you do not sound; you do not need to sound like an American speaker or a British speaker. But if you are able to utter every sound clearly, neutralizing it without interfering of your mother tongue, and you are done.  You do not have to sound like any other person; your own style is sufficient to make an impression on people. Now, you also need to understand little things about sounds of English, sound patterns of English. For example, vowels in English, long and short vowels. So, the length of a vowel does make a difference in meaning, so gate versus get, weight versus wet, west versus waist, beach versus bitch, peas versus piss.  So, look at the long vowels; they make a difference; you have to be very particular, there are languages where this difference may be problematic because of the mother tongue interference. So, Bangle for that matter or other Indian languages we do have problem with length of the vowel. So, you need to understand that in English, length of a vowel is a very serious thing. In English length of the vowel is phonemic.  It makes a difference in the meaning. So, you need to understand appropriate sound and also the nature of the sounds. I do not want you to become proficient in understanding the structure of language and syllable and all those things will help you minimize the blunders and mistakes that we make while speaking while we speak.  Vocabulary forms the fundamental basis for any language and learning; vocabulary learning is a very complex phenomenon. It does not refer to. Vocabulary does not refer to a single word, it may be a chunk of words giving us complete sense, and vocabulary learning is complete with mastering three aspects.  Number one, form, the word, structure of the word, spelling and word, then meaning the concept encoded in the word, and third is the context in which it is used. So, we do not only learn a language in, a word in isolation; we learn a word with three components, a structure of the word, meaning of the word and context of the word. So, where it is used, that makes you a proficient user and speaker in the language.  Then, structure and fluency are equally important, and if you go by David Crystal, a very renowned linguist, he says that grammar is a structural foundation of our ability to express ourselves, the more we are aware of how it works, the more we can monitor the meaning of effectiveness of the way we and others use language.  It can help foster precision, detect ambiguity and exploit the richness of expression available in English, and it is true to any language, not only English, it is true to all languages. So, we need to develop little mastery over structures. So, fundamental rules and functional rules of English. For example, English sentences cannot drop the subject; that is a very fundamental rule.  In Hindi, we can drop the subject; in most of the Indian languages, we have the tendency of dropping the subject, but in English, you cannot drop the subject, and if at all, the verb is impersonal, and the subject is dropped, we have a replacement and that is called expletives it or there. So we say it is raining, we do not say raining, is raining, it is raining, it has no meaning.  But it occupies the subject position to complete the sentence; there was a king, you cannot was a king, there was a king. So, in Indian languages, you may not require expletives or this kind of structure to occupy the subject position and also those languages where you have a very rich vocabulary, where the verb contains all other grammatical information, then we have this option of dropping the subject.  In English, we can drop the subject only in one context, and that is imperative sentences and that too because the subject of all imperative sentences is one, and that is you. So, imperatives sentences, like orders, commands, advice, that requests, helping. So, if you look at the deep structure, if you go down, it is you help me, you, please help me.  So, you can be dropped. Help me. Get out, come in, you come in, you get out. So, get out, come in, take medicine on time, you take medicine on time. So, imperative sentences allow the subject to be dropped, and the reason is the recoverability. We can understand who is the subject, what is the subject, what occupies the subject position, it is known it is recoverable. So, it allows, otherwise know where you dropped the subject.  So, understanding little grammar helps a lot and in this course, I am sure you are familiar with fundamental functional grammar and categories. So here, you have to use them. You have to practice them. Another important factor in good speech, speaking is fluency, and repeatedly I have been telling the same thing, fluency does not mean high speed or uncommon words or low-frequency words.  Fluency in communication refers to pace and flow in articulation uninterrupted. Not the rate of the delivery, normal pace and normal flow, but it should not have interruptions at the level of idea, it should go in a flow. So, you are fluent; you should not look like making an effort to make it fluent; when the moment you start speaking with a relaxed posture and without obviously making effort, you are fluent.  A steady rate of production of speech, holds the attention of the speaker and comprehension happens without any impediment or obstacle. So, if you have steady speed, not too high, not too low, too high, omits a lot of information to low reduces the deducts the interest of your audience. So, you have to maintain a normal flow and a steady flow and that is sufficient.  You might have come across a lot of people speak at a very high speed and your audience feels tired, difficult to follow them, you feel tired, some people speak very slow. So, you feel exhausted and bored. So, you have to strike a balance, you do not have to speak at a very high speed at the same time, not so low that your audience is exhausted.  There are certain communications strategies we have to follow basic norms like greetings, You're opening of the talk, turn-taking and turn-giving. So, you should in interactive communication or in a group meeting, we should have this courtesy of giving turn and also in capitalized on taking turn. So, it is turn-taking turn-giving, and it is a negotiated thing which happens between the communication partners.  Holding the floor means what you say is logical rational, and you have arguments to drive your point home. Paraphrase, if you are using some complex idea, clarify if you find that your audience is not following you, being relaxed composed, maintaining a steady flow and an animated voice, you need to maintain appropriate body language you should not look stiff, tense, stressed and aggressive.  And you should develop the ability of interpreting the feedback, your audience may not give you oral feedback all the time, but sometimes their body language, the way they look at you, their gaze there stare, their body language, their presence, they all give you a clue, you have to understand the cues and clues that you get from the audience and interpret the feedback and accordingly customize your delivery. That is important.  So, there are certain characteristics we need to understand in English. This is not an exhaustive list, but some basic fundamental thing I wanted to mention, like elision and assimilation, we just discussed it, fast train. The fast first word has T sound at the end and the train, the second word has the T sound at the beginning, in a connected speech, when you speak, it is assimilated. Fast train.  Sometimes speakers have this tendency of making contracted forms and weak forms of vowel. All speakers have their own idiosyncrasies, their own style and also idiosyncrasies. When we speak, we had the tendency of hopping from one idea to the other without completing the sentence. So, you will have many times half finished sentences, so while listening to them, you should understand and while speaking, you have to keep in mind these things. Then tactic elements like demonstrative pronounce this, that there, those, they all have different application, there are a times they are pronounced at certain places they become adjective.  So, we have to think about that, understand them. Discourse markers. So, when we speak and interact, we have lots of fillers, you know, well, just a minute, precisely, absolutely. So, these are discourse markers, which signal your engagement in the interaction but not necessarily carry the lexical content. So, you have to understand them. There are words like then, so, but, they are also used to organize your thoughts.  So, not necessarily they are particular grammatical unit or a word with a particular grammatical function, no, sometimes and, then, so, but, such words are used as an anchor, to recollect and organize your thought. So, you have to develop those kinds of skills as well. The usual speed is 120 to 150 words per minute. But anything above 100 words per minute is sufficient, in a very good flow. So, do not worry about it, do not try to speak too much in too little time, take your time, speak fluently, take your time, and 100 words per minute is sufficient.  Now, we need to understand certain useful expressions. So, as a beginner in English, if you are using, so you have to develop certain phrases and utterances, how to begin for that matter, how to put things in order for that matter, how to signal a change for that matter, in the interaction. Now, I will move to XYZ, I will conclude with XYZ, I will end by the XYZ. So, this signal, the change of your idea.  How to order arguments? So, firstly, in the first place, the first thing I want to say, I would like to discuss this, secondly, thirdly, lastly. So, that orders our argument, how to end, so we can see that, to sum up, we need to take it into consideration in short and we continue. So, this is how we end our idea.  How to express opinion? So, in my opinion, or as I think, I believe, this is how we go about it. Signalling choice, so agreeing, disagreeing, it has to be done politely and certain sentences and words signal that you agree, certain sentences and words signal we do not agree. So, I hope, I make sense, but at the same time and then can you do something like, I do understand, but I think that and then, so you are disagreeing. So, this is how we need to develop such expressions.  Turn -taking and turn-giving. This is my opinion. But what do you think, giving the turn to the other person. Do you agree to the fact that, and then you are giving turn, or you can directly say, what is your opinion about it? But do you think and then, that means you are signalling a turn giving, you are giving the turn to your communication partner, do not you think, and then you are giving done.  So, turn-taking turn -giving and finally, last but not least, finally, in the professional domain, you need to look tidy, prepared, confident. So, you have to groom yourself. Effectively speaking does not mean only language and word. It is an overall package. So, you have to also work on your personal aspects. Your appearance, I am not talking about physical attributes.  I am not talking about your color, your hairstyle and everything. No, I am talking about how tidy you look, how organized you look, how prepared you look, look at that adds to your confidence and also the confidence of your audience. You need to look sincere, you need to look thorough, easily accessible, friendly, and flexible, and you need to understand and interpret the non-verbal cues of the audience.  So with all these, we can make our presentation, our discussion, our interaction and public speech effective, and you can be an effective speaker of English and an effective user of English and these are not very complicated things. This is not rocket science. It is an art. You need to inculcate develop, and it will come to you gradually with practice. So, thank you very much for the day.

title: Developing Communication Skills
text: English – II Dr Om Prakash Guest Faculty, Humanities and Social Sciences Indian Institute of Technology Madras, Chennai, Welcome to class. Today we are going to talk about the fundamental of communication skills. Communication is an overused term. We all understand it, we all do all the time, but today in this class, we talk about fundamental nature of communication, human communication system and what are the skills required to be a good communicator, an effective communicator, what are the things that we need to develop and what are myths about communication. Usually See we believe that somebody who speaks at a very high speed, the pace of delivery is very high, somebody who uses, let us say, very ornamental and complex sentences or somebody who is using very low-frequency words, low-frequency words, I mean, words which are not usually used in everyday conversation, we consider that person to be an effective or an eloquent speaker. But speaking too much, speaking at a very high speed or speaking low-frequency words using complex structures, long sentences, they are not characteristics of effective communication. Because always remember the communication has communicability, the essence of the message which is received by your listener, by your receiver, that counts. It does not matter how great speaker you are, it does not matter how eloquent speaker you are, but if you are not able to communicate your idea to ordinary people or to anyone whom you want to communicate with, or your receiver does not interpret and receive your message, communication does not happen. So, it is not about the complexity of sentences. It is not about low-frequency words, it is not about very sophisticated style of speaking, it is not about speaking in a fake accent, sounding like an American, or a British or a native speaker, it is about translating your ideas into sentences and communicating those ideas in easily understood sentences to your audience that is important. So, in all communication event, the speaker is important, but the most important person is your partner in communication, the receiver, so communication is you-centric, not I-centric if you are not able to understand then does not matter how beautifully I speak, how eloquently I speak, what kind of complex sentences I am using. So, communication has to take place only when, and it takes place only when your message is delivered and received by the receiver without any distortion and ambiguity. So, today we are going to talk about how to develop effective communication skills, and I am not going to talk about rocket science, I am not going to tell you A-B-C or step 1, step 2 or step 3 of developing communication skills. I will be talking about very common, general things most of you are familiar, but it is kind of reinforcement, so I will be just mentioning and underlining those factors which you may already be knowing so look at communication.  It is the fundamental human need and which enables us to share, and it is a sharing in terms of our thoughts, ideas, emotions, intelligence, and information which we possess, and this is what help us survive and evolve as a person, as a society, as a race. So, that is very significant.  With changing time and space, communication challenges, communication needs have also changed. Today our challenges are different, and so are the means of addressing them. But what remains the same is the role and relevance of communication in the course of human survival and success. So, communication is central to our everyday activities; I mean, everything that we do, anything that we do, it happens where the communication is at the center. So, the centrality of communication, this is what I want to underline.  Now, if you look at the fundamental premises of communication. See communication has an objective, it has a goal; it is not done without purpose. Every communication has a goal, a need; it is done with a purpose. So, we need to understand the motive, the goal, the objective, the process, procedure and the outcome of this entire communication event. So, we communicate with a purpose, and it is a two-way process. It is not a one-way process; it is a two-way process. So, when we say two-way process, that means when you communicate, you have a partner to communicate with. So, when you send a message, somebody receives it; sending happens only when it is received and receiving happens only when something is being sent. So, it is always a two-way process, so that is the first fundamental premise of communication. Can we consider any sending of the signal and receiving of the signal, sending of the message and receiving of the message as an event of communication? No. There must be exchange and progression of ideas; that is a second premise. And the third is mutually accepted goals. So, goal of communication must be mutual. There must be continuity, exchange and progression, and it has to be a two-way process. So, this is how communication happens. So, there are three fundamental premises we need to understand; it has to be a two-way process then only communication happens; there has to be an exchange, exchange of what, exchange of messages and feedbacks. So, when I am sending a message to you, I receive feedback, feedback ensures that you have received a message and also decoded it appropriately without any ambiguity, so intended message has reached to you, so it ensures, your feedback ensures that. So, communication, the second premise is exchange of message and feedbacks and progression in a certain direction, and the goal of communication of both the partners must be mutually accepted. So, this is how we understand the fundamental premises of communication.  Moving on, then when we say effective communication, what are the things which make communication effective? As I told you, communication is not about the speed of delivery, good communication is not about using complex sentences, long sentences, effective communication is not about using low-frequency words or literally ornamental sentences; it is about being relaxed, composed using simple sentences where the message is important, not the format, content is important. So, when we look at the content of communication, it must be brief. And what do you mean by brief? Brevity is a character of good communication that means your message must be succinct, precise and to the point, straightforward and to the point. If you have excessive access of words and complex sentences, saying repetitive sentences, saying the same thing in different words, repeating, it somehow brings your impact down. So you need to be very brief, you need to be very clear, you need to be very objective, so the message must focus on the content, it must be objective and being objective means it does not allow your audience to interpret openly. It detects ambiguity and does not allow your audience to have multiple meanings out of it. You need to understand that creative writing is different from let us say professional writing, why? Because creating writing gives a lot of imaginative space to the audience, it is open-ended, the text is open-ended, open for interpretation, but in professional domain we cannot have this luxury of allowing the audience to have open interpretations and ambiguity and multiple meanings, deriving multiple meanings out of it. So, it has to be objective, straightforward and precise, being simple is the most challenging thing. Because we have this tendency of making things complex unnecessary, that is not required. So, you need to be simple and when say simple, you need to have simple sentences, small sentences, appropriate pauses, full stops, commas, punctuation marks so that it does not give a lot of cognitive load to the audience, to your readers and listeners to interpret what you want to say. The pace for that matter, the tempo for that matter, must be appropriate and slow. It is not required to speak in a very fluent and high-speed delivery; you do not have to deliver in speed, it has to be appropriately paused at places and tempo must be slow, speed must be appropriate, and you have to customize it, you have to adjust it as per the need of your audience, we cannot afford to have the same style everywhere. Your style is customized, your approach is customized, your messages customized according to the need of your audience and as a speaker and as a writer or as a user of language you need to understand the need of your audience. Always remember you are communicating, talking, or writing not for yourself; you are involving another partner, your audience, your reader, your listener, so the message must be clear. It must be simple; it must be objective and precise. Intelligible: An effective communication is intelligible, easy to comprehend, so it does not give challenges to the audience to understand it, it does not give challenges to the reader to understand it because then you lose the purpose, you fail in that if you are not able to make it intelligible and easy to comprehend. And finally, most importantly, it has some value for your audience, so what you are saying, what you are writing, it must carry certain value attached to it. It must be useful, because we receive a lot of messages every day, but we do not allow, assign equal value to all of these, so we filter which message is important for me, so unless your message is useful or has certain values for the audience they will not receive a message. So, in order to be effective communicator you need to learn this art of being brief, being clear, being objective, being precise, being simple, being intelligible and message being useful. These are attributes to effective communication.  Moving on, then what language skills are required, what language skills are required to be a good communicator? So, there are four, there are four integrated language skills, and we say integrated because they are not independent skills, they are integrated and as a whole, they make you effective communicator, so what are these? L, S, R, W. Four. L stands for listening, S stands for speaking, R stands for reading, and W stands for writing. Why do we call it integrated skills? Because these skills appear in this order naturally, and when you acquire even your first language, your mother tongue, you start with listening, input, and then speaking, output. So, there is a myth that listening is a passive skill, it is not a passive skill, reading is a passive skill, it is not a passive skill, speaking is active, writing is active, listening and reading are passive. Listening is very active skill, but it is this receptive in nature, you receive, so you actively receive it, so we call it receptive skill. Similarly, reading is also very active skill, because you may look idle while reading, but actually your mind is not idle; it is very active, and very much active and hyper, but you receive the input, so reading gives input, which is manifested in your writing that is active skill. So, listening is receptive, speaking is active, reading is receptive, and writing is active. So, there are four integrated skills, and we need to polish, hone our skills in all these four areas to become a better communicator and to become a better user of the language. So, by no means listening is less productive; speaking is of course productive, obviously it is perceptible; we can see, we can observe. But listening is equally active but receptive; we receive the input, so listening is input-oriented, speaking is output-oriented. Similarly, reading is input oriented and writing is output-oriented. So, we need to understand this integration of these skills and be better communicator. So, in order to become a better communicator, we have to have good listening skills, then only it will feed into the speaking, speech production. Similarly, you have to have a very good reader to have appropriate input for your writing and orthographic productions, so you need to understand the importance and significance of all these four skills and all these four skills are equally important to be a better user of language. Unfortunately, the way we have been educated in our schools, we have learned English grammar in class, listening and speaking skills were hardly given a chance to practice. So, we focused more on reading and writing. But two skills were ignored, but at this stage, in your professional domain, you need to be a good speaker and for good speaking, you cannot avoid this, or you cannot ignore the significance of listening. Similarly, you need to give a lot of writing output in a professional domain, but you cannot undermine the significance of reading to improve your writing skills.  We will come to each of these skills by and by, but let us move on to listening skill. How to improve your listening skills? So, one is called active listening. What is active listening? That means you are actively engaged with the speaker, you are following the utterances, sentences, you are continuously receiving and decoding it, you are able to understand it with attention and concentration. You need to understand the accent of your speaker; not all of us speak in a similar accent. We all have our own style, our own diction style, are own renditions. We all have different style of speaking, but that is the beauty of human mind and that is the beauty of human language that despite these idiosyncrasies and individual-centric language characteristics, we are able to decode, we are able to understand each of them. Sometimes accent can be challenging for you because if the English speaker is a native speaker for that matter, the speed will be very-very high for you as in non-native user of language. So the non-native user of language will have little challenges in understanding the accent of different speakers, so we need to pay attention to understanding various accents, European, American, Canadian, or Indian English is definitely different. The speed, our speed is a little slower compared to the native speakers, so you need to understand the accent, number one. Number two, you need to understand the word boundaries and its structure. So, what do you mean by word boundary? In a flow, in connected speech, we have lots of elision and assimilation of sounds. And sometimes, if you are not very attentive, and if your ears are not tuned and trained, it would be difficult for you to understand and identify individual words. So, you have to train your ears, tune your ears to understand such assimilation of sound, such elision and understand the word boundary, where one word ends and other word begins, you need to focus on that, and you need to tune in understanding different accents and different pace of delivery. Then you need to understand connected speech. In writing, you can see full stop, you can see a comma, you can see a colon, you can see a dash, you can see a hyphen, so these punctuation marks are orthographically presented. You can see them, and you can understand the word boundary; you can understand because words are written separately, each word is separate, space and then and then other word.  So this space between two words allow you to understand the word boundary, but it does not happen in listening, because pauses can give you a clue about sentence boundary, pauses can give you a clue about clause boundaries, but not the word boundary, and specifically when the speaker is native speaker or somebody who is well competent in English and speaking to you fluently. So, you need to understand the connected speech, these boundaries and lots of elision a d assimilation that happens in there. Then speed is another problem, while listening speed is another problem. Possibly with lots of attentive sessions, you give to yourself, and lots of tuning in with the sounds of English and also understanding the pace of delivery of the speakers gradually you will cope up the speed of delivery. Then you need to understand the details of the content. What content is being delivered? You need to understand the detail and for that, you need to understand the tone, so the segmental and super-segmental features, you need to understand the sounds, you need to understand the combination of sounds and words. You need to understand the word boundaries and phrases, you need to understand the phrases and clauses, and sentences, where the one sentence ends another sentence begins, content, the meaning of it, so you need to understand the detail of it to be a good, effective, emphatic listener. Furthermore, you need to understand overlapping speeds. So, 3 – 4 people are talking at the same time around you, or you may be one of them, so it is never the case like radio transmitter where was one person says, “Charlie over,” then other person begins. In connected speech, in an interactive setting, in a group, when you communicate you will have lots of overlap, not only that you will have overlap within the speaker as well because one idea overlaps with the other, one sentence overlaps with the other sentence. Sometimes your half-finished sentences, so you need to understand these overlaps; you need to understand the context in which the text is being used. Then the cross-cultural information, a lot of cross-cultural information, intonation for that matter, discourse markers for that matter or fillers for that matter, you have fillers all the time. So, then style of different speakers, and you need to understand a range of topics, so you need to do all these things, and they will come to you gradually, nothing to worry, but you need to do a lot of practice in that, and for that you need to be exposed to a variety of sample speech speakers with different background and gradually your ears will be tuned. You will be able to understand accent, elision, assimilation, connected speech, speed, so it will help you develop your listening skills and become an emphatic and active listener.  Moving on to the next skill that is speaking so, it is a productive skill, and it is very dynamic and productive skill. So, you have to focus on how to speak intelligibly, clearly. How your sounds are clear? Again I repeat, speaking good English does not mean speaking like an American or speaking like a British, you do not have to speak like anyone, you use English the way you want to use it and there is no inhibition. You should not be embarrassed if you are not able to speak like an American or British. You have your own style and let me tell you every speaker has his or her own style, so you do not have to sound like an American or a British or some other native speaker, mind you, English is not your native language, so do not be embarrassed, be confident. What is most important is speaking intelligibly. So, what you are speaking must be clear to everyone who is listening to you, It does not matter what accent are you use, this is your own style, use it and be confident. Speaking fluently, but fluency does not mean speed; fluency does not mean speaking many words per minute; speed is not important.  What is important? The continuity of your idea, if your idea, your thoughts, your content is continuous without a break and if your audience is able to follow you without interruption in idea, you are fluent, if you are not making obvious efforts, perceptible efforts, observable efforts, if you are appearing effortless, if you look effortless and speak at your own speed and intelligibly and confidently, you are a good speaker. You do not have to have high speed of the thing, your tempo must be appropriate, pitch must be alright and that is it. So, you do not have to sound like anyone, you own it and derive pride out of it that you can speak intelligibly without interruption fluently. Fluency refers to the continuity of idea and the content, not the speed of delivery, pace of delivery. Then paraphrasing, paraphrasing is an art, when you are talking to somebody, when you are giving a public speech, when you are making a presentation, or you have a group of people following you, listening to you, you will get feedback that what you said may not be understood by them the way you intended originally to be understood. And in that case you need to paraphrase it, you need to repeat it in a different word, differently, elaborate it; that is the sign of a good and confident speaker when you can elaborate what you want to say in many ways, in multiple ways, to suit the need of your audience and for that you do not need to make a lot of effort. You will get the signal from your audience; you will get the feedback from your audience that they are not able to follow you, and in that case you need to paraphrase. Then we need to up employ a lot of, and employ a lot of communication strategies. We will talk about such strategies later on, but strategies like connecting with your audience, giving them space, making yourself accessible and flexible. Looking effortless and engaging with them, responding to them quickly, and it becomes very evident in the face to face interaction. In your professional domain you may have to appear for interviews that is, so there you need to have interactive skills. You may have to give many presentations, short term, short time, extempore presentations. You can speak fluently when you have this ability to form opinion, look at things, observe them, understand them and form opinion; then only you can express them effectively. In your job settings, possibly you may have some group discussion or formal presentation, so for that, you need to be ready, and you can be ready only by looking at these small things.  They are not a rocket; this is not rocket science; only thing is that you need to identify the areas where you need to work on and there are so many resources available now that will help you develop your speaking skills.  Moving to the next skill, developing reading skills, as I told you reading is very active skill. So, the moment you look at a text we get some idea, idea like what this text is all about, what kind of text is this, what it may contain, so your thought process begins before you have started actually reading the text, so pre-reading skills where you are able to see, understand and guess broadly the text and anticipate what is coming. While-reading, that means, when you read, your thought process also follows the text, sometimes the reading can be slower than your thought process because we quickly reconstruct what is coming off, we anticipate the next thing coming up and that increases the speed of your reading. Post-reading exercises, which means post-reading, after the text is over, actually you have completed the text, but the text is not over in your mind. It is continuing, so lots of assimilation goes in, and you develop your opinion, your thoughts about the text, about the contents of the text, so this engagement with the text starts before you start reading the text, it continues while you read the text, and it is followed up after you finish reading the text and that is a gradual process, it comes to you slowly depending on how intensely you read and how frequently you read, how much time you devote in reading.  There are two things, the two styles of reading, the skimming and scanning. Skimming refers to reading without a preconceived notion where you just skim through the text and get to know what is there in the text. Scanning refers to an anticipated preconceived idea with which you approach the text and exactly identify that information you are looking for. Deduction refers to the overall reduction that you make after reading. So, in order to become a good communicator, you have to have a very wide range of reading, you have to have good speed of reading, you have to have this art of engaging with the text and making deductions out of it.  Then we move to writing skills. So, after listening, speaking and reading, though all the three above give you a lot of feedback and input to your writing production and for writing there are certain things we need to be prepared with, like a wide range of vocabulary. You have to have fairly good command on high-frequency words and when we say high-frequency words that mean the words which are used frequently around you in everyday life. And also, domain-specific words, we call them jargon, so if you are talking in term, technically, or you are making a technical presentation, discussing a technical issue, you must be familiar with the jargon and the technical words used in that domain. Then you have to have this command on structures, grammatical structure, so you should be familiar with grammar, you do not have to be master of grammar, but you have to be good enough in translating your ideas into simple structures.  How to do that? You must be able to choose from a wide range of available words, which word fits into a particular context, so appropriate of selection you must be familiar with. So, you have to organize while writing; before writing you have to organize ideas, what exactly you want to write, collecting your ideas, then organizing them, and then we engage in drafting and then editing. When you draft something, you must be reading it from the readers perspective and see if there is any gap, see if there is any punctuation marks gap because a single, or a hyphen, or a colon can make a difference in meaning and always remember written text speaks for itself and writer is not there to explain, so the reader is free to interpret. So, in order to limit the distortion and ambiguity in your text, it must be punctuated appropriately, so full stops, commas, dash, colons must be placed appropriately. The selection of word is also very important. So, words must be selected carefully so that they carry the intended message appropriately, so they fit into the context and carry your intended message effectively. Paragraphing – So, paragraph, in each paragraph one central idea is called nucleus sentence. So, every paragraph has a nucleus sentence and all the arguments are built around it. So, when you change the idea, you must change a paragraph, so you must make another paragraph. So, paragraph tells you the flow of idea and in each paragraph we have one nucleus sentence and all other sentences are qualifiers. They elaborate the idea and make it a single meaningful unit. So, you have to have this art of paragraph. And of course, everyone, and all of us are an individual user of language. So, we all have our own style of writing, speaking, we all have our own style of choosing a particular word for a particular context. But what guides them, what governs this whole selection is the appropriate, structural appropriate, semantic appropriate, meaning appropriate, depending on the intended message it must be structurally appropriate and semantically appropriate so that your message is encoded appropriately and the receiver or the reader of your text is able to interpret the text the way you want the reader to interpret. So, it comes with a lot of practice. So, these are fundamentals of effective communication, and towards the end et us quickly understand that being a good communicator requires, does not require you to speak at a very high speed or use low-frequency words or use ornamental language or have complex sentences, it is all about being simple, precise, clear, intelligible and effective. And little practice, a little awareness and consistency makes you a good communicator. So, this is for now. Thank you very much.

title: Write Well
text: English II Ms Parthia Sathyanathan Humanities and Social Sciences Indian Institute of Technology Chennai Hello all, I welcome you to this class. In today's class, we will discuss writing. So, we will look at the different stages involved in the process of writing a good piece of literature.  So, when I say a good piece of literature, I mean to say that you can use this particular strategy known as power writing when you write essays, when you write letters, emails, business reports, blog posts, stories, novels, etc. So, what is power writing? It is actually an acronym for prepare, organize, write, evaluate and review, which are the five stages of writing. We will discuss each stage in detail, and I want you to do the activity simultaneously as you go through this video.  Now, the first stage is called prepare. So, one of the major reasons why we often struggle to write is because we lack enough ideas, we do not have enough ideas with us, and therefore we end up writing anything and everything that comes to our mind. So, coming up with good points or collecting all your ideas before you write is a very important step.  Now, this entire process of ideating or preparing, sitting and thinking about the good points related to the essay question, or it could be email any kind of writing is, that whole process is known as brainstorming. Now, I will tell you what are the different methods or what are the different steps involved in brainstorming.  One is that you have to note down anything that comes to your mind. Now here, if you are a perfectionist, you are going to be very critical about your ideas. Please do not do that. Note down all the points that come to your mind. Do not leave out or discard anything, thinking maybe this is not right, maybe this is not good enough. Do not worry about organizing your ideas at this point; we will do that in the later stage.  So, you are just going to write everything that comes to your mind is ideas in this particular stage, which is known as prepare. Again, when you are jotting down your ideas. Please do not worry about grammar, spelling, pronunciation, etc. and keep jotting down and keep noting them in a rough work, in a rough paper, until you exhaust all your ideas, until you have no more ideas. So, this is the first part of it.  Now, I am going to give you an activity, write a letter of requisition to return your caution deposit for library books. So, let us suppose you are, you have appeared for your final semester exam, and now it is time for you to graduate. So, write a letter to the librarian. What kind of letter, a letter of requisition, what is the letter of requisition, when you write a letter to somebody asking or requesting for service of some kind of help, then it is known as a letter of requisition.  So, in this letter of requisition, I want you to write about returning your caution deposit which is 2000 rupees that you had entrusted earlier as a part of the book reading scheme. So, now with what we have discussed so far, which is the first stage known as prepare, I want you to come up with all the ideas, everything that you could use to write this particular letter. Please do that. Pause the video; work on this. Work on ideating and brainstorming, and then we will go to the next stage.  Now, the next stage is known as organizing. In this stage, you need to outline what you are going to write, so throughout this stage it is very important to ask yourself, how am I going to guide my reader. So, think of yourself as a tour guide, who would want the tourists to visit place A followed by place B and then play C and finally conclude the entire visit with something interesting, with some interesting piece of information.  So, think of yourself as a tour guide and ask yourself what should your reader read first? Then what should your reader read next and what should the reader read last, this is very important part organizing, your ideas need to be organized properly and thoroughly. So, from the ideas that you have collected, Now select the best ones; now is the time to filter. Sometimes it so happens that you have fascinating ideas, some good ideas, but then it does not fit in the entire scheme of, the scheme of writing.  So, it is important that at those moments, however interesting is the point is, or however good the point is, you will have to leave it out; you will have to strike it off. So, organizing part of this particular stage is very important, and you need to ask yourself what your reader should read first, next and last. Now, once you filter and select the best ones, arrange the ideas in a logical sequence. This is very important, arranging your ideas in a logical sequence.  Now, the same activity, I suppose in the last part of this video, you had worked on the first stage of writing the requisition letter, which is preparing; I want you to organize those ideas. Ask yourself what you should write first, what you should write next and then what you should write last.  Now comes the third stage, which is known as write. Now that you have all the ideas and the ideas are organized in a logical sequence. You should now take your ideas in your outline and write full sentences for them. Treat this as a first draft. So, do not worry about spelling, punctuation, vocabulary grammar; in first draft, you do not look at those things. In the next stage, we will look at evaluating and correcting the mistakes.  So at this point, write full sentences; while writing, it also happens that you come up with additional ideas, or you might feel like you should remove something, or you should feel like you know, maybe I should organize it a little differently, and you might want to move your ideas around. That is all fine. That is all perfect. It is a natural process. It happens to everybody.  So, you do not have to panic at that point thinking, oh my god, I am not sticking to the stages. So, the procedure that is known as the power writing, so you should not worry about that. If you think that there are additional ideas that come in the last moment, you can definitely add them in this particular stage as well.  Now, coming to the activity, write a letter of requisition to return your caution deposit for library books; you have already done that with the two stages that is prepared and organize. Now, I want you to write full sentences; your ideas need to be converted to full sentences and organized in a logical sequence. So, please do that; I have written a sample here.  Now, comes the fourth stage which is evaluated. So, this is where you proofread your work, or this is where you check for mistakes, your spelling mistakes or grammar mistakes or punctuation mistakes. So, at this stage, you need to look at the vocabulary; you need to ask yourself if you can replace certain words with better words, if there can be a better choice of words. Then you need to check for spelling mistakes, grammar mistakes and finally the punctuation mistakes.  And in this particular stage, I have corrected some of the mistakes that I have made in the previous stage, which is the writing stage. If you see I have written student book loan scheme, it is a scheme. So, it should; it should start with a capital letter. So, S should be in caps, B should be in caps, and L should be in caps.  Similarly, I have paid 2000, it is always better, you write I have paid Rs 2000 and also look at it, I have made a mistake in the spelling of semester, and the final mistake is, please write back to me. There can be a better usage, so I have marked that as a mistake, and I would like to change that in the next stage, which is evaluated.  And in evaluating stage, I write, I request you to make arrangements for the refund at the earliest and then thanking you sincerely. It is a formal letter, it is a request letter. So, you need to be very formal and polite in your writing.  And finally comes the review stage; it is always a good idea to go over your work one final time. This is to make sure that writing has the intended effect on the reader, and if it is a long piece of work, do not review it immediately. If you have written a novel, it is always better than to keep it for a couple of days and then come back, because your mind would be fresh, and you will have more ideas, and you will be able to review or proofread it in a better way.  Now, reading out loud, reading your writing out loud to check whether it sounds natural, is also an important step. Sounding natural is very important, and if you can ask someone to read it, if you can suggest your friend to read it and give you feedback, that would be a great idea too, that can actually improve your writing. So with this, we come to the end of the session. I hope you like the session. I will meet you with a different topic on a different day. Until then, stay safe. Take care, bye.

title: Developing Writing Skills
text: English – II Professor D r. Om Prakash Guest Faculty, Humanities and Social Sciences Indian Institute of Technology, Madras Welcome to class. Today we are going to talk about how to develop a good writing skill. As you are familiar, we have four integrated language skills. So, when I say I know Hindi, when I say I know English, when I say I know Tamil, I know Telugu, I mean to say that I have proficiency, linguistic proficiency in terms of listening or understanding, speaking, reading and writing. So, four integrated skills, listening, speaking, reading and writing, that is the natural order. Writing comes at the end of the list. That means, writing comes very late to us in our childhood as compared to listening and speaking. Listening and speaking are primary fundamental skills. Why? Because languages are primarily oral, and we acquire our mother tongue naturally, but reading and writing are crafted skills. We acquire these skills of reading and writing in a language with a structured instruction and conscious and cautious effort.  So we have to make a lot of effort to learn the script because the script is at the center of these two skills, reading and writing. So, as a user of language, we have to be familiar with the script and scripts are taught separately. You acquire listening and speaking, two skills, without any structured instruction from the environment; but you acquire even reading and writing in your own mother tongue with instructions, structured instructions. That is the difference between these two sets of skills. And that is why we need to pay extra effort in understanding, reading, and writing. Let us say in English, which is not your mother tongue, it is second or third language to you. So, you need more effort to develop this skill. You may be a good speaker of English, you may be a good listener. You can understand the text very easily. But when it comes to writing, it is a productive skill; it requires a lot of other complex cognitive skills to accomplish a good task of writing. And that is why we are going to talk about writing as a skill and how we can develop this skill.  So, in this talk, we are going to talk about certain widely held ideas to develop skills. I repeat, there is no golden rule, and you might come across claims where people say ‘10 golden rules to write good English ’. I do not know, there is no Golden Rule. You need a lot of continuous effort and practice, and how to go about it ? What are the background preparations we need to make? What do we need to do while writing? Post-writing, what do we need to do? How, what is the follow-up? So, all these basic fundamental general things we are going to talk about but at the same time, if you want to develop your writing skill, you need to engage with the language and the activity, and you need to have a lot of practice. Now, there are certain prerequisites. As I told you, that this is a well-crafted skill inculcated or acquired with the help of structured instructions in a formal setup. So usually, as a human child, we learn to read and write when you go to school or even at home, then in this structured supervision of the adults. So, extending this understanding into a second or third language definitely will require a lot of effort on your part. So just be ready for that and believe me, you can develop a very good skill in writing. And there are certain prerequisites, that means background preparations before you start writing. Certain basic elements you need to have, linguistic units you need to have, before you start, or get to serious writing. First and foremost, we need of course, we need to understand that script, and we need to understand the alphabet, that is the separate thing. This is a minimum, bare minimum basic thing; we will not talk about that. But given the fact that as an Indian user of English, we are all familiar with functional grammar, we are all familiar with a wide range of vocabulary, we are familiar with spelling of the word. So, I assumed that we have those ingredients and the background linguistic units that are required for writing. But if you are engaged in good writing, serious writing, you need to have a range of vocabulary, wide range of vocabulary, so to develop a wide range of vocabulary. Then you have to have fairly good command on grammar. And when we say fairly good command on grammar, I do not mean you to be a grammarian, who knows all the rules. That is not required, but you are required to be able to formulate sentences. So, you are able to understand the basic functional grammar, so that you can formulate grammatical sentences in English. So, a fairly good range of vocabulary, a fairly good command on functional grammar and ability to formulate sentences, grammatical sentences, acceptable sentences. These are three primary requirements. Beyond that, at a little higher level, you need to be understanding the context. Because always remember, any word or any text has meaning within a context, not outside. So, when you learn a word, you do not only, you not only learn to spell of it or pronunciation of it, you learn a word in terms of three aspects of learning. The three aspects of learning involved in a word, particular word, and every word that you learn, there are three aspects of learning involved. Number one, you learn the spelling, or the pronunciation of the word, that means the structure of the word. So, you need to learn a structure of the word. That is the first thing. Then you need to learn meaning of the word. So structure, meaning, the second aspect. And what is the third aspect? Context in which it is being used, or it is used. So when we learn a word, we learn three things together about a word, and then only that word learning is complete. Most of us go by dictionary entries. Dictionary entries suggest a basic meaning of the word, basic idea about the word, but words are used in a text or in a sentence in a particular context.  It can be metaphorical use, it can be idiomatic use of the words. So word literally means the same in the dictionary entry, but if you look at the sentence, it may give you a different meaning. And that is why understanding the extended use of the word is important. And interestingly, in Indian English, for that matter, we write or speak with extended meaning of these words and most of the time, even the native speakers of English fail to derive sense out of it because you need to be familiar with the cultural context. You need to be familiar with not only structure and meaning but also the context, cultural, social cultural context. And you need to understand the variation in the structure and variation in the meaning. So, your understanding is complete when you understand a word in terms of its structure, its meaning, and its context. And that is why good reading, extensive reading is required to discover the contexts of use of a particular word. So, you need to understand the context, then most of the time you find it difficult to map the idea and the text, that means translate your ideas into the text. English is not your mother tongue, we are not native speakers of English. As we are not native speakers of English, we have a lot of socio-cultural gaps in our understanding of the language. So, translation becomes little problematic for us and we need to learn that art. So, you have to practice a lot for translating your ideas into actual acceptable Standard English sentence. And there is no golden rule for that. Let me repeat myself again and again, that you need to do practice, you need to have practice, and extensive reading in terms of input and frequent practice of writing in terms of output.  Then only this skill will develop.  So, then every text has a structure. So, you have to have the central idea of the text, then all the required information must be organized in chronological order. So, the text should be, or the following sentences should be in the feeding order to complete the sentence. We have a lot of cohesive devices, a lot of connectors that we use in English.  Then punctuation is a very serious thing in the text, written text. And why? Because, a single comma, comma denotes a pause; colon, again denotes a pause; semicolon also denotes a pause; full stop is complete pause. So, you have to understand however for that matter, inverted commas, where to put the inverted commas. So, you have to understand punctuation. In orals format of the language, you do not have to be familiar with the use of comma or full stop everything, your pauses work. If I have a long pause, it means sentence is complete, sentence is complete. So, we play with the pauses, we play with supra segmental ideas or features like you know, intonation, stress, rhythm. But these are missing in written text, because written text is different from oral text. So, the sounds are missing, and the supra segmental features are missing. So, in the text, you have black and white orthographic symbols. So, all these sup segmental features and the variations and the pitch and everything is represented in terms of punctuation. So, you have colons, commas, semicolons, inverted commas, dash, hyphen.  You need to understand the role of these in writing. Of late you can see that people use, the majority of people in the majority of writings, they use two things, comma and full stop. Now you have italics and bold and underlined features because of typing. But you need to be familiar with proper punctuation.  Paragraphing? Paragraphing is about organizing your idea in the text. Each paragraph that you write contains a central idea. Every paragraph is centered around a singular idea. And in that paragraph, you have a nuclear sentence, and rest of the sentences of the paragraph are like qualifying statements. So, it has to be argumentative. And when your argument ends, or the new idea begins, it is always advisable to have a paragraph. That helps you in organizing your idea in a chronological order. Again, stylistic choices.  All of us use language, according to our own style and fancies. So, we all have our own unique style of using language. We all speak differently, with a different style. We all have our own idiosyncrasies in language and that is also reflected when you write.  So, your personal imprint is there in the text you write. So, the choices you make, choices of words, choices of sentences, choices of arrangement, it can be deductive, it can be inductive. So, these stylistic choices are purely yours, you have to develop your own style of writing, and that becomes a trademark. So, these are the prerequisites in developing good writing skills. Quickly summing up, you need to develop wide range of vocabulary; you need to have fairly good command on grammar, functional grammar; you do not have to be grammarian, you do not have to remember rules of grammar, not at all. But a functional use of it, you should be familiar with the functional use of grammar.  You should be able to formulate grammatical sentences.  You need to understand the text and the context. Furthermore, you need to develop skills of translating and mapping your ideas into linguistic structures; organizing your idea, avoid repetitions because in writing that is kind of immortal, permanent thing. When you speak, we do a lot of repetition and paraphrasing. When we speak, we have a lot of half-finished sentences.  We seem casual at times, we drop linguistic elements but in writing, we cannot afford to do so. So, you have to have complete grammatical sentences and a complete sentence within two full stops. So, you have to have the skill to use cohesive devices, how to connect sentences, how to connect long sentences, how to make complex sentences.  Always remember, writing complex sentences, ornamental sentences are not good sign of a good writer. A good writer is one who is able to communicate the central idea of the text without interruption and ambiguity. So, you are not into essay writing competition or a creative writer where you have to show off your writing skills.  You are not writing poetry. You are not writing novels. Furthermore, you can afford to write this when you get to that level, and you can write poetry, you can write novels. But always remember those novels and those portrait connect the audience, or all of us, if we do not have to make extra effort to understand that. So, if they are intelligible and easily comprehensible. So, it is the content which is important in your text, not the ornamental complex style of writing. So do not be influenced by this idea of writing complex sentences, long sentences, bringing in low-frequency words, people do not understand the meaning of it. So, you can use simple language, high frequency words.  You can have simple sentences.  Still you can be profound in your meaning. So, so, that is the art of writing.
